Built with Google ADK 2.0 (`gemini-3.8-flash`), stateful tools, and built-in A2A serving. """ from typing import Any, Dict from google.adk.agents import Agent from google.adk.agents.callback_context import CallbackContext from google.adk.apps import App from google.adk.models import Gemini from google.adk.tools.tool_context import ToolContext from google.genai import types MODEL = "gemini-3.8-flash" TICKET_DB: Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]] = { "TCK-1042": { "customer": "Acme Cloud Robotics", "tier": "enterprise", "severity": "P1", "status": "open", "summary": "Production payment webhook returning HTTP 503 timeouts in eu-west1.", }, "TCK-2088": { "customer": "Northwind Retail", "tier": "standard", "severity": "P3", "status": "investigating", "summary": "CSV invoice export omits localized tax column.", }, } SLA_POLICIES: Dict[str, Dict[str, str]] = { "enterprise": { "P1_response": "15 minutes", "P2_response": "1 hour", "P3_response": "4 hours", "dedicated_oncall": "Yes (24/7 SRE pager)", }, "standard": { "P1_response": "2 hours", "P2_response": "8 hours", "P3_response": "24 business hours", "dedicated_oncall": "No (business-hours queue)", }, } def initialize_support_state(callback_context: CallbackContext) -> None: """Initializes default session and user state keys before the first turn.""" # TODO 1: Initialize `callback_context.state["user:customer_tier"] = "standard"` # and `callback_context.state["escalated_tickets"] = []` if those keys are not already present. pass def lookup_ticket(ticket_id: str, tool_context: ToolContext) -> Dict[str, Any]: """Looks up an enterprise support ticket by ID and syncs customer tier into state. Args: ticket_id: Ticket identifier such as 'TCK-1042' or 'TCK-2088'. """ norm_id = ticket_id.strip().upper() # TODO 2: Look up `norm_id` in `TICKET_DB`. # - If missing, return a dict with `"status": "not_found"`, `"ticket_id": norm_id`, # `"available_sample_tickets": sorted(TICKET_DB.keys())`, and an informative `"message"`. # - If found, store `record["tier"]` in `tool_context.state["user:customer_tier"]`, # store `norm_id` in `tool_context.state["active_ticket_id"]`, and return # `{"status": "found", "ticket_id": norm_id, **record}`. pass def check_sla_policy(tier: str) -> Dict[str, Any]: """Returns response-time SLA targets for a customer tier ('enterprise' or 'standard'). Args: tier: Customer support tier ('enterprise' or 'standard'). """ norm_tier = tier.strip().lower() # TODO 3: Look up `norm_tier` in `SLA_POLICIES`. # - If missing, return `{"status": "error", "message": ...}`. # - Otherwise return `{"status": "success", "tier": norm_tier, "sla_targets": policy}`. pass def escalate_ticket( ticket_id: str, reason: str, tool_context: ToolContext, ) -> Dict[str, Any]: """Escalates a high-severity support ticket to the incident engineering queue. Args: ticket_id: Ticket identifier to escalate (e.g., 'TCK-1042'). reason: Concise technical justification for the escalation. """ norm_id = ticket_id.strip().upper() # TODO 4: Validate `norm_id` exists in `TICKET_DB` (return `{"status": "error", ...}` if unknown). # Append `norm_id` to `tool_context.state["escalated_tickets"]` (avoiding duplicates), # route `"enterprise"` tier tickets to `"24/7 P1 SRE Oncall"` (otherwise `"Tier-2 Engineering Queue"`), # and return `status`, `ticket_id`, `assigned_queue`, `reason`, and `session_escalated_tickets`. pass # TODO 5: Define `root_agent = Agent(...)` with: # - `name="support_ops_agent"` (matching `root_agent_name` in `agents-cli-manifest.yaml`) # - `model=Gemini(model=MODEL, retry_options=types.HttpRetryOptions(attempts=3))` # - `before_agent_callback=initialize_support_state` # - Clear operational `instruction` referencing `{user:customer_tier?}` that directs the agent to: # 1. Call `lookup_ticket` first when given a ticket ID, # 2. Call `check_sla_policy` for the ticket's customer tier, # 3. Call `escalate_ticket` if severity is P1 or escalation is requested, # 4. Summarize ticket status, SLA target, and escalation queue. # - `tools=[lookup_ticket, check_sla_policy, escalate_ticket]` root_agent = None # Replace with Agent(...) # TODO 6: Wrap `root_agent` in `app = App(root_agent=root_agent, name="app")` # CRITICAL: `name="app"` MUST match `agent_directory: "app"` in `agents-cli-manifest.yaml`! app = None # Replace with App(...)

Author the evaluation dataset in tests/eval/datasets/basic-dataset.json: Replace the contents of support-ops-agent/tests/eval/datasets/basic-dataset.json with three representative support scenarios (P1 escalation, standard SLA lookup, and graceful unknown-ticket handling): { "eval_cases": [ { "eval_case_id": "p1_ticket_triage_and_escalation", "prompt": { "role": "user", "parts": [ { "text": "Investigate ticket TCK-1042, check its SLA target, and escalate if required." } ] } }, { "eval_case_id": "standard_ticket_sla_lookup", "prompt": { "role": "user", "parts": [ { "text": "What is the current status and applicable SLA response target for ticket TCK-2088?" } ] } }, { "eval_case_id": "unknown_ticket_graceful_handling", "prompt": { "role": "user", "parts": [ { "text": "Please check the status of ticket TCK-9999." } ] } } ] } Execute your baseline evaluation run: agents-cli eval run (Note: Managed built-in metrics in eval grade call the Gemini platform Evaluation Service using your Google Cloud ADC project. documents.t: Before moving to Cloud Run deployment in Module 32, match each enterprise requirement below to its optimal agents-cli deployment target and protocol strategy (cloud_run, agent_runtime, gke, or A2A on cloud_run): Scenario 1 — Startup MVP: A seed-stage startup needs to ship an e-commerce support agent for a pilot customer by Friday with zero Kubernetes staff, instant HTTPS, and scale-to-zero cost efficiency. Scenario 2 — Regulated Public-Sector Workload (FedRAMP): A defense contractor needs a strictly auditable, FedRAMP-compliant internal compliance agent with zero-config managed sessions and OAuth 2.0 user consent in Gemini Enterprise. Scenario 3 — Quantitative FinTech Mesh (GPU + Custom NetworkPolicy): A financial institution runs all workloads inside an existing Kubernetes platform requiring GPU node pools and strict pod-to-pod NetworkPolicy isolation. Scenario 4 — Cross-Organization Partner Integration: Two external partner organizations need their autonomous procurement agents to discover your agent's capabilities dynamically via /.well-known/agent-card.json and invoke tasks over standard JSON-RPC HTTPS on serverless infrastructure. Check your code and scenario selections against lab-solution.md or the Reference Solution Vault below!

🔐 Official Solution Vault — Module 31 Locked Challenge — Active Pedagogical Socratic Gate Step 1/3: Question 1 of 3 When bootstrapping an ADK Python project with 'agents-cli scaffold create support-ops-agent --agent adk --prototype', what rule governs App(name=...) in app/agent.py? ✨ [ACCESS GRANTED] Solution Vault Decrypted Congratulations on completing all checks and the terminal challenge! Here is the official reference walkthrough and architecture review: 🎉 Challenge Lab Unlocked! Record this lab as completed in your study plan? ✓ Mark as Complete Lab 31 Solution: Prototyping, Testing & Evaluating with Google Agents CLI Goal​ This reference solution contains the exact CLI workflow, complete runnable app/agent.py implementation, evaluation dataset, and architectural scenario answers for Module 31. Step 1: Scaffold & Environment Setup​ uv tool install google-agents-cli agents-cli setup --skip-auth cd /path/to/your/adk-training agents-cli scaffold create support-ops-agent \ --agent adk \ --prototype \ --agent-guidance-filename GEMINI.md cd support-ops-agent agents-cli info app/agent.py​ """ Enterprise Support Operations Agent — Canonical Part 6 End-to-End Agent (`agents-cli`). Built with Google ADK 2.0 (`gemini-3.8-flash`), stateful tools, and built-in A2A serving. """ from typing import Any, Dict from google.adk.agents import Agent from google.adk.agents.callback_context import CallbackContext from google.adk.apps import App from google.adk.models import Gemini from google.adk.tools.tool_context import ToolContext from google.genai import types MODEL = "gemini-3.8-flash" TICKET_DB: Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]] = { "TCK-1042": { "customer": "Acme Cloud Robotics", "tier": "enterprise", "severity": "P1", "status": "open", "summary": "Production payment webhook returning HTTP 503 timeouts in eu-west1.", }, "TCK-2088": { "customer": "Northwind Retail", "tier": "standard", "severity": "P3", "status": "investigating", "summary": "CSV invoice export omits localized tax column.", }, } SLA_POLICIES: Dict[str, Dict[str, str]] = { "enterprise": { "P1_response": "15 minutes", "P2_response": "1 hour", "P3_response": "4 hours", "dedicated_oncall": "Yes (24/7 SRE pager)", }, "standard": { "P1_response": "2 hours", "P2_response": "8 hours", "P3_response": "24 business hours", "dedicated_oncall": "No (business-hours queue)", }, } def initialize_support_state(callback_context: CallbackContext) -> None: """Initializes default session and user state keys before the first turn.""" if "user:customer_tier" not in callback_context.state: callback_context.state["user:customer_tier"] = "standard" if "escalated_tickets" not in callback_context.state: callback_context.state["escalated_tickets"] = [] def lookup_ticket(ticket_id: str, tool_context: ToolContext) -> Dict[str, Any]: """Looks up an enterprise support ticket by ID and syncs customer tier into state. Args: ticket_id: Ticket identifier such as 'TCK-1042' or 'TCK-2088'. """ norm_id = ticket_id.strip().upper() record = TICKET_DB.get(norm_id) if not record: return { "status": "not_found", "ticket_id": norm_id, "available_sample_tickets": sorted(TICKET_DB.keys()), "message": f"Ticket '{norm_id}' was not found.", } tool_context.state["user:customer_tier"] = record["tier"] tool_context.state["active_ticket_id"] = norm_id return {"status": "found", "ticket_id": norm_id, **record} def check_sla_policy(tier: str) -> Dict[str, Any]: """Returns response-time SLA targets for a customer tier ('enterprise' or 'standard'). Args: tier: Customer support tier ('enterprise' or 'standard'). """ norm_tier = tier.strip().lower() policy = SLA_POLICIES.get(norm_tier) if not policy: return { "status": "error", "message": f"Unknown tier '{tier}'. Valid tiers: enterprise, standard.", } return {"status": "success", "tier": norm_tier, "sla_targets": policy} def escalate_ticket( ticket_id: str, reason: str, tool_context: ToolContext, ) -> Dict[str, Any]: """Escalates a high-severity support ticket to the incident engineering queue. Args: ticket_id: Ticket identifier to escalate (e.g., 'TCK-1042'). reason: Concise technical justification for the escalation. """ norm_id = ticket_id.strip().upper() if norm_id not in TICKET_DB: return {"status": "error", "message": f"Cannot escalate unknown ticket '{norm_id}'."} escalated = list(tool_context.state.get("escalated_tickets", [])) if norm_id not in escalated: escalated.append(norm_id) tool_context.state["escalated_tickets"] = escalated tier = tool_context.state.get("user:customer_tier", TICKET_DB[norm_id]["tier"]) queue = "24/7 P1 SRE Oncall" if tier == "enterprise" else "Tier-2 Engineering Queue" return { "status": "escalated", "ticket_id": norm_id, "assigned_queue": queue, "reason": reason.strip(), "session_escalated_tickets": escalated, } # Keep name="support_ops_agent" in sync with root_agent_name in agents-cli-manifest.yaml root_agent = Agent( name="support_ops_agent", model=Gemini( model=MODEL, retry_options=types.HttpRetryOptions(attempts=3), ), before_agent_callback=initialize_support_state, instruction=( "You are the Support Operations Agent (active customer tier: {user:customer_tier?}).
" "Follow this exact operational workflow:
" "1. When given a ticket ID, ALWAYS call `lookup_ticket` first.
" "2. Call `check_sla_policy` for the ticket's customer tier so your answer cites exact SLA response times.
" "3. If a ticket has P1 severity OR the user requests escalation, call `escalate_ticket` with a concise technical reason.
" "4. Summarize the ticket status, applicable SLA target, and any escalation queue clearly." ), tools=[lookup_ticket, check_sla_policy, escalate_ticket], ) # CRITICAL for agents-cli: App `name` MUST match `agent_directory: "app"` in agents-cli-manifest.yaml app = App( root_agent=root_agent, name="app", ) tests/eval/datasets/basic-dataset.json​ { "eval_cases": [ { "eval_case_id": "p1_ticket_triage_and_escalation", "prompt": { "role": "user", "parts": [ { "text": "Investigate ticket TCK-1042, check its SLA target, and escalate if required." } ] } }, { "eval_case_id": "standard_ticket_sla_lookup", "prompt": { "role": "user", "parts": [ { "text": "What is the current status and applicable SLA response target for ticket TCK-2088?" } ] } }, { "eval_case_id": "unknown_ticket_graceful_handling", "prompt": { "role": "user", "parts": [ { "text": "Please check the status of ticket TCK-9999." } ] } } ] } Steps 3 & 4: Verification & Quality Flywheel Commands​ # Install & lint agents-cli install agents-cli lint # Multi-turn stateful smoke test agents-cli run "Investigate ticket TCK-1042 and check its SLA." --start-server --session-id demo-1 agents-cli run "Which customer tier was stored in my profile, and was TCK-1042 escalated?" --session-id demo-1 agents-cli run "Stop" --stop-server # Run baseline evaluation & diff against a candidate run agents-cli eval run # After refining prompt/instructions and running `agents-cli eval run` a second time: # agents-cli eval compare artifacts/grade_results/<baseline>.json artifacts/grade_results/<candidate>.json Step 5: Architecture Target Selection Answers​ Scenario 1 — Startup MVP → cloud_run (agents-cli scaffold enhance . --deployment-target cloud_run) Justification: Cloud Run delivers the fastest serverless container rollout with automatic HTTPS, IAM/IAP options, and scale-to-zero billing (--min-instances 0 by default in dev) so the startup pays nothing during idle periods without managing Kubernetes clusters. Scenario 2 — Regulated Public-Sector Workload (FedRAMP) → agent_runtime (agents-cli scaffold enhance . --deployment-target agent_runtime) Justification: Agent Runtime in Gemini platform is the managed deployment target providing built-in FedRAMP compliance, automatic VertexAiSessionService persistence, CMEK support, and native OAuth 2.0 user consent when registered with Gemini Enterprise. Scenario 3 — Quantitative FinTech Mesh (GPU + Custom NetworkPolicy) → gke (agents-cli scaffold enhance . --deployment-target gke) Justification: GKE Autopilot (or Standard) integrates directly into an existing Kubernetes ecosystem while supporting custom GPU node pools, fine-grained Kubernetes NetworkPolicy rules, and full Pod-level resource and sidecar control. Scenario 4 — Cross-Organization Partner Integration → Built-in A2A on cloud_run Justification: Every Python ADK project scaffolded by agents-cli automatically exposes an A2A AgentCard (/a2a/app/.well-known/agent-card.json) and JSON-RPC endpoint via app/app_utils/a2a.py. Deploying that container to Cloud Run gives external partner agents standards-based cross-org discovery and invocation on elastic serverless infrastructure (and supports --registration-type a2a in Gemini Enterprise). Self-Reflection Answers​ Why does changing App(root_agent=root_agent, name="app") to name="support_ops_agent" break agents-cli run and agents-cli eval when the code lives inside app/agent.py? Answer: ADK's FastAPI server and agents-cli's evaluation generator resolve /apps/{app_name}/... routes against the agent package directory (agent_directory: "app"). If App.name diverges from "app", session creation and SSE invocation look up different application keys, resulting in "Session not found" errors. Why should behavioral assertions live in agents-cli eval datasets rather than pytest unit tests? Answer: pytest is deterministic and ideal for testing pure Python contracts (e.g., verifying lookup_ticket("tck-1042") normalizes casing), whereas LLM phrasing and multi-step tool trajectories are probabilistic. agents-cli eval uses rubric-based LLM judges (final_response_quality, multi_turn_tool_use_quality, multi_turn_task_success) that evaluate semantic correctness and tool usage without flaking on minor wording variations. Why does agents-cli recommend starting with --prototype and running scaffold enhance only after your core eval dataset passes? Answer: --prototype keeps the workspace focused on app/agent.py and tests/eval/ while requirements and tool designs are still fluid. Once agents-cli eval run proves the agent meets its quality bar, scaffold enhance cleanly layers Terraform, CI/CD workflows, and load tests in place without premature DevOps overhead.

""" Enterprise Support Operations Agent — Canonical Part 6 End-to-End Agent (`agents-cli`). Built with Google ADK 2.0 (`gemini-3.8-flash`), stateful tools, and built-in A2A serving. """ from typing import Any, Dict from google.adk.agents import Agent from google.adk.agents.callback_context import CallbackContext from google.adk.apps import App from google.adk.models import Gemini from google.adk.tools.tool_context import ToolContext from google.genai import types MODEL = "gemini-3.8-flash" TICKET_DB: Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]] = { "TCK-1042": { "customer": "Acme Cloud Robotics", "tier": "enterprise", "severity": "P1", "status": "open", "summary": "Production payment webhook returning HTTP 503 timeouts in eu-west1.", }, "TCK-2088": { "customer": "Northwind Retail", "tier": "standard", "severity": "P3", "status": "investigating", "summary": "CSV invoice export omits localized tax column.", }, } SLA_POLICIES: Dict[str, Dict[str, str]] = { "enterprise": { "P1_response": "15 minutes", "P2_response": "1 hour", "P3_response": "4 hours", "dedicated_oncall": "Yes (24/7 SRE pager)", }, "standard": { "P1_response": "2 hours", "P2_response": "8 hours", "P3_response": "24 business hours", "dedicated_oncall": "No (business-hours queue)", }, } def initialize_support_state(callback_context: CallbackContext) -> None: """Initializes default session and user state keys before the first turn.""" if "user:customer_tier" not in callback_context.state: callback_context.state["user:customer_tier"] = "standard" if "escalated_tickets" not in callback_context.state: callback_context.state["escalated_tickets"] = [] def lookup_ticket(ticket_id: str, tool_context: ToolContext) -> Dict[str, Any]: """Looks up an enterprise support ticket by ID and syncs customer tier into state. Args: ticket_id: Ticket identifier such as 'TCK-1042' or 'TCK-2088'. """ norm_id = ticket_id.strip().upper() record = TICKET_DB.get(norm_id) if not record: return { "status": "not_found", "ticket_id": norm_id, "available_sample_tickets": sorted(TICKET_DB.keys()), "message": f"Ticket '{norm_id}' was not found.", } tool_context.state["user:customer_tier"] = record["tier"] tool_context.state["active_ticket_id"] = norm_id return {"status": "found", "ticket_id": norm_id, **record} def check_sla_policy(tier: str) -> Dict[str, Any]: """Returns response-time SLA targets for a customer tier ('enterprise' or 'standard'). Args: tier: Customer support tier ('enterprise' or 'standard'). """ norm_tier = tier.strip().lower() policy = SLA_POLICIES.get(norm_tier) if not policy: return { "status": "error", "message": f"Unknown tier '{tier}'. Valid tiers: enterprise, standard.", } return {"status": "success", "tier": norm_tier, "sla_targets": policy} def escalate_ticket( ticket_id: str, reason: str, tool_context: ToolContext, ) -> Dict[str, Any]: """Escalates a high-severity support ticket to the incident engineering queue. Args: ticket_id: Ticket identifier to escalate (e.g., 'TCK-1042'). reason: Concise technical justification for the escalation. """ norm_id = ticket_id.strip().upper() if norm_id not in TICKET_DB: return {"status": "error", "message": f"Cannot escalate unknown ticket '{norm_id}'."} escalated = list(tool_context.state.get("escalated_tickets", [])) if norm_id not in escalated: escalated.append(norm_id) tool_context.state["escalated_tickets"] = escalated tier = tool_context.state.get("user:customer_tier", TICKET_DB[norm_id]["tier"]) queue = "24/7 P1 SRE Oncall" if tier == "enterprise" else "Tier-2 Engineering Queue" return { "status": "escalated", "ticket_id": norm_id, "assigned_queue": queue, "reason": reason.strip(), "session_escalated_tickets": escalated, } # Keep name="support_ops_agent" in sync with root_agent_name in agents-cli-manifest.yaml root_agent = Agent( name="support_ops_agent", model=Gemini( model=MODEL, retry_options=types.HttpRetryOptions(attempts=3), ), before_agent_callback=initialize_support_state, instruction=( "You are the Support Operations Agent (active customer tier: {user:customer_tier?}).
" "Follow this exact operational workflow:
" "1. When given a ticket ID, ALWAYS call `lookup_ticket` first.
" "2. Call `check_sla_policy` for the ticket's customer tier so your answer cites exact SLA response times.
" "3. If a ticket has P1 severity OR the user requests escalation, call `escalate_ticket` with a concise technical reason.
" "4. Summarize the ticket status, applicable SLA target, and any escalation queue clearly." ), tools=[lookup_ticket, check_sla_policy, escalate_ticket], ) # CRITICAL for agents-cli: App `name` MUST match `agent_directory: "app"` in agents-cli-manifest.yaml app = App( root_agent=root_agent, name="app", )

{ "eval_cases": [ { "eval_case_id": "p1_ticket_triage_and_escalation", "prompt": { "role": "user", "parts": [ { "text": "Investigate ticket TCK-1042, check its SLA target, and escalate if required." } ] } }, { "eval_case_id": "standard_ticket_sla_lookup", "prompt": { "role": "user", "parts": [ { "text": "What is the current status and applicable SLA response target for ticket TCK-2088?" } ] } }, { "eval_case_id": "unknown_ticket_graceful_handling", "prompt": { "role": "user", "parts": [ { "text": "Please check the status of ticket TCK-9999." } ] } } ] }

In Module 31, you built support-ops-agent, verified stateful tool execution locally, and proved its quality with agents-cli eval run. Now you are ready for Phases 5 and 6 of the agents-cli lifecycle: upgrading your prototype in place for Google Cloud Run (scaffold enhance) and rolling out a live, authenticated HTTPS container (agents-cli deploy). Google Cloud Run is a fully managed serverless container runtime that pairs naturally with ADK agents: Zero Server Administration: Provide a Dockerfile (already generated by agents-cli), and Cloud Run manages TLS certificates, load balancing, health checks, and revision rollouts. Dual-Protocol Serving Out of the Box: The scaffolded uvicorn app.fast_api_app:app container simultaneously serves ADK's native streaming routes (/run_sse, /apps/app/...) and the Agent-to-Agent (A2A) surface (/a2a/app/.well-known/agent-card.json + JSON-RPC) on port 8080. Pay-Per-Request & Revision Traffic Control: Dev services scale to zero when idle (--min-instances 0), while production services pin warm instances and support instant traffic shifting across immutable revisions.

documents.t: Figure: Automated Cloud Run promotion pipeline — in-place IaC enhancement, Cloud Build image compilation, Artifact Registry storage, and Cloud Run revision rollout. Because you started with --prototype in Module 31, adding Cloud Run infrastructure requires zero code rewrites. Running scaffold enhance from inside support-ops-agent/ merges production assets in place while preserving app/agent.py, .env, GEMINI.md, and tests/eval/ untouched: agents-cli scaffold enhance . \ --deployment-target cloud_run \ --cicd-runner github_actions \ --region us-central1 What scaffold enhance Adds to Your Project​ Updated agents-cli-manifest.yaml: Records deployment_target: cloud_run, cicd_runner: github_actions, and region: us-central1 so agents-cli deploy knows how to package and target the service. Modular Terraform IaC (deployment/terraform/): deployment/terraform/single-project/ (service.tf, iam.tf, storage.tf) — Single-project Cloud Run v2 service, Artifact Registry, least-privilege app_sa runtime service account, and telemetry bindings (usable via agents-cli infra single-project --apply). deployment/terraform/cicd/ & deployment/terraform/shared/ — Multi-environment staging-to-production promotion with cicd_runner_sa, Workload Identity Federation (WIF), and optional persistent Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL 15 session storage when --session-type cloud_sql is selected. CI/CD Pipelines (.github/workflows/ or .cloudbuild/): Automated lint, evaluation gate, staging deploy, load test, and human-approved production rollout workflows. Load Testing Suite (tests/load_test/load_test.py): Pre-configured Locust harness for stress-testing concurrency and memory ceilings before production launch.
documents.s: Upgrading a Prototype In Place with agents-cli scaffold enhance

documents.t: For rapid dev and staging deployments, agents-cli deploy works standalone (no prior terraform apply required) and exposes fine-grained sizing and security flags: Flag Default (agents-cli deploy) Production Guidance & Coupling Rules --cpu 1 Container runs a single async Uvicorn process; scale out via concurrency and instances first, raising --cpu only when profiling shows real CPU saturation rather than LLM wait time. --memory 4Gi Memory bounds concurrency. Each concurrent request holds its prompt history, tool payloads, and stream buffer in RAM (peak ≈ base + concurrency × per-request RAM). Never raise --concurrency without checking --memory. --concurrency 8 Conservative default protecting RAG/multimodal agents from OOM. Lightweight tool-calling agents can tune to 16–32 using tests/load_test/load_test.py. --min-instances 0 (1 in service.tf) 0 avoids idle dev cost; pass --min-instances 1 (default in generated service.tf) to eliminate cold starts for latency-sensitive or Live API agents. --max-instances 10 Horizontal scaling cap protecting downstream APIs and model quotas. --timeout 300 (seconds, max 3600) Increase to --timeout 3600 for long-running research workflows or bidirectional Live / voice WebSocket sessions. --iap Off Enables Identity-Aware Proxy on Cloud Run so only authorized Google Workspace identities can reach the service without custom auth code. --secrets — Mounts GCP Secret Manager secrets as env vars (e.g., --secrets "WEBHOOK_TOKEN=prod-webhook:latest"); never commit production API secrets into .env.
documents.s: Sizing, Security & Secrets Flags on agents-cli deploy

documents.t: One of the most important operational distinctions on Google Cloud is separating where your container runs from where your Gemini model endpoint is served: DEPLOY_REGION (--region us-central1): Cloud Run services, Cloud Build workers, and Artifact Registry repositories are regional resources and require a concrete region such as us-central1 or europe-west1. GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION=global: On Gemini Enterprise / Vertex AI (GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_ENTERPRISE=1), gemini-3.8-flash is served on the global endpoint. Passing --env-vars "GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_ENTERPRISE=1,GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION=global" ensures the running Cloud Run container routes model inference to global rather than defaulting to us-central1 (which would cause runtime 404 NOT_FOUND model errors): export GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT="your-project-id" export DEPLOY_REGION="us-central1" agents-cli deploy \ --project "$GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT" \ --region "$DEPLOY_REGION" \ --env-vars "GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_ENTERPRISE=1,GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION=global" \ --no-confirm-project
documents.s: Separating Infrastructure Region (DEPLOY_REGION) from Model Location (GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION=global)

documents.t: By default, Cloud Run services deployed by agents-cli enforce IAM authentication (--no-allow-unauthenticated). Rather than manually crafting curl headers and minting short-lived identity tokens, agents-cli natively authenticates, manages sessions, and speaks both protocols against your --url: Test the Built-In A2A Endpoint (--mode a2a): Discovers /a2a/app/.well-known/agent-card.json and streams JSON-RPC tasks over HTTPS: agents-cli run "Investigate ticket TCK-1042 and check SLA." \ --url "$SERVICE_URL" \ --mode a2a Test the Native ADK Streaming Endpoint (--mode adk): Creates an ADK session and streams Server-Sent Events (/run_sse) against --app-name app: agents-cli run "Check ticket TCK-2088." \ --url "$SERVICE_URL" \ --mode adk \ --app-name app Run Remote Cloud Evaluation (eval generate --url + eval grade): Validates the live Cloud Run container end-to-end against tests/eval/datasets/basic-dataset.json: agents-cli eval generate --url "$SERVICE_URL" --app-name app && agents-cli eval grade 🎯 Knowledge CheckSelect Best Answer When deploying 'support-ops-agent' ('gemini-3.8-flash') to Cloud Run in 'us-central1' using 'agents-cli deploy', why do you pass '--region us-central1' together with '--env-vars GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_ENTERPRISE=1,GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION=global'? ACloud Run services can only be created in a region literally named 'global'BCloud Run infrastructure requires a concrete region like 'us-central1' ('--region'), while 'GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION=global' tells the container's google-genai SDK to call 'gemini-3.8-flash' on the global enterprise endpoint instead of 'us-central1' (preventing 404 NOT_FOUND errors)CPassing 'GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION=global' disables IAM authentication and TLS encryption on the Cloud Run URLDIt converts the Cloud Run container into a stateful Cloud SQL database instance Check Answer 💡 Need a Hint?
documents.s: Testing & Evaluating Live Cloud Run Endpoints

documents.t: In-Place Promotion (scaffold enhance): agents-cli scaffold enhance . --deployment-target cloud_run upgrades a validated prototype with Terraform IaC (deployment/terraform/), CI/CD pipelines, and Locust load tests without touching app/agent.py or .env. Coupled Sizing: Memory (--memory, default 4Gi) bounds --concurrency (default 8); scale --concurrency, --memory, and --max-instances together using tests/load_test/, and set --min-instances 1 (plus --timeout 3600 for Live voice agents) when cold starts are unacceptable. Region Separation: Always pair regional Cloud Run infrastructure (--region us-central1) with --env-vars "GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_ENTERPRISE=1,GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION=global" for gemini-3.8-flash. Live Dual-Protocol Verification: Use agents-cli run --url "$SERVICE_URL" --mode [a2a|adk] and agents-cli eval generate --url "$SERVICE_URL" --app-name app && agents-cli eval grade to verify authenticated Cloud Run deployments end-to-end.

In this lab, you will carry support-ops-agent (gemini-3.8-flash) from its local prototype into production on Google Cloud Run using the agents-cli Golden Path: enhancing the project in place with Cloud Run Terraform & CI/CD scaffolding (scaffold enhance), deploying with clean infrastructure-vs-model region separation (agents-cli deploy), querying both its built-in A2A and ADK SSE endpoints live in the cloud, and grading evaluation traces generated directly from the deployed Cloud Run URL. Environment setup: 1-Click Launch (Browser): Open in GitHub CodespacesOpen in Google Cloud Shell Local machine: If you're continuing the course in sequence, cd into the adk-training project you created in Module 2 and skip the block below -- your environment and dependencies already carry forward. If you're starting fresh at this module, create that project first: uv init adk-training --python 3.10 && cd adk-training uv add "google-adk>=2.1.0" python-dotenv DevContainer / Codespaces (Alternative): If you opened this repository in a DevContainer or GitHub Codespaces, Python 3.11, uv, gcloud, and all core ADK dependencies are pre-installed in your container environment.

A Google Cloud Project with billing enabled and Owner or Editor permissions. Google Cloud CLI installed and authenticated: gcloud auth login gcloud auth application-default login gcloud config set project YOUR_PROJECT_ID Enable the required Google Cloud APIs in your project: gcloud services enable \ run.googleapis.com \ cloudbuild.googleapis.com \ artifactregistry.googleapis.com \ aiplatform.googleapis.com \ secretmanager.googleapis.com \ --project=YOUR_PROJECT_ID google-agents-cli installed (uv tool install google-agents-cli).

Continuing from Module 31? Simply enter your existing support-ops-agent/ directory: cd /path/to/your/adk-training/support-ops-agent agents-cli info Starting fresh at Module 32? Run this 10-second standalone bootstrap from adk-training/ (do not mkdir support-ops-agent beforehand) to pull the canonical app/agent.py and evaluation dataset: cd /path/to/your/adk-training agents-cli scaffold create support-ops-agent --agent adk --prototype --agent-guidance-filename GEMINI.md curl -fsSL https://mauripsale.github.io/doc-adk-training/samples/part6/agent.py -o support-ops-agent/app/agent.py curl -fsSL https://mauripsale.github.io/doc-adk-training/samples/part6/basic-dataset.json -o support-ops-agent/tests/eval/datasets/basic-dataset.json cd support-ops-agent Verify that app/agent.py defines root_agent (name="support_ops_agent", MODEL = "gemini-3.8-flash") and app = App(root_agent=root_agent, name="app"), and that root_agent_name: support_ops_agent is set in agents-cli-manifest.yaml.

Upgrade support-ops-agent in place to add Cloud Run Terraform modules, GitHub Actions CI/CD workflows, and Locust load tests while leaving app/agent.py and .env completely intact: Export your project ID and Cloud Run region, then run scaffold enhance: export GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT=YOUR_PROJECT_ID export DEPLOY_REGION=us-central1 agents-cli scaffold enhance . \ --deployment-target cloud_run \ --cicd-runner github_actions \ --region "$DEPLOY_REGION" agents-cli install Inspect the generated production artifacts: agents-cli-manifest.yaml: Confirm deployment_target: cloud_run, cicd_runner: github_actions, and region: us-central1 are recorded. deployment/terraform/single-project/service.tf: Inspect the google_cloud_run_v2_service definition, including min_instance_count, max_instance_request_concurrency, CPU/memory limits, and the runtime app_sa service account. tests/load_test/load_test.py: Review the generated Locust load test used to benchmark concurrency and latency under load. app/agent.py: Confirm your stateful support_ops_agent code was preserved untouched!

documents.t: Now package, build, and deploy the container to Cloud Run in us-central1 while pointing GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION inside the container to the global Gemini Enterprise / Vertex AI endpoint for gemini-3.8-flash. Preview the exact deployment command with --dry-run: agents-cli deploy \ --project "$GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT" \ --region "$DEPLOY_REGION" \ --env-vars "GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_ENTERPRISE=1,GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION=global" \ --no-confirm-project \ --dry-run Inspect the printed gcloud command to see how agents-cli configures --memory 4Gi, --cpu 1, --concurrency 8, --min-instances 0, and your runtime environment variables. Execute the live Cloud Run rollout: agents-cli deploy \ --project "$GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT" \ --region "$DEPLOY_REGION" \ --env-vars "GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_ENTERPRISE=1,GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION=global" \ --no-confirm-project Wait 2–4 minutes while Cloud Build builds the uv-managed Dockerfile, pushes the image to Artifact Registry, and rolls out the Cloud Run revision.

documents.t: Capture the live Cloud Run SERVICE_URL: SERVICE_URL=$(gcloud run services describe support-ops-agent \ --region="$DEPLOY_REGION" \ --project="$GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT" \ --format='value(status.url)') echo "Live Service URL: $SERVICE_URL" Test the live Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocol endpoint (--mode a2a): agents-cli automatically attaches your Google Cloud identity token, fetches $SERVICE_URL/a2a/app/.well-known/agent-card.json, and invokes the agent over A2A JSON-RPC: agents-cli run "Investigate ticket TCK-1042 and check SLA." \ --url "$SERVICE_URL" \ --mode a2a Verify that the cloud service looks up TCK-1042, cites the 15 minutes enterprise P1 SLA, and escalates to 24/7 P1 SRE Oncall! Test the live ADK SSE streaming endpoint (--mode adk): agents-cli run "Check ticket TCK-2088." \ --url "$SERVICE_URL" \ --mode adk \ --app-name app Verify that it returns the status (investigating) and standard P3 SLA (24 business hours) for Northwind Retail. Run remote cloud trace generation + automated grading against the live URL: Drive the evaluation dataset from tests/eval/datasets/basic-dataset.json directly against your deployed Cloud Run container and grade the captured traces: agents-cli eval generate --url "$SERVICE_URL" --app-name app && agents-cli eval grade Inspect the printed score summary and the new artifacts/grade_results/results_<timestamp>.html report to confirm parity between local and cloud execution!

documents.t: Under the Hood Reference: adk deploy cloud_run, Instant Traffic Rollback & Cleanup When working on standalone single-folder ADK experiments outside an agents-cli repository, the core ADK CLI also offers uv run adk deploy cloud_run, which synthesizes a temporary Dockerfile and runs gcloud run deploy: # Standalone ADK CLI alternative (for non-scaffolded single-agent folders): uv run adk deploy cloud_run \ --project="$GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT" \ --region="$DEPLOY_REGION" \ --env GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION=global \ app/ Instant Cloud Run Revision Rollback (Zero-Commit Recovery): While GitOps rollback (reverting a commit on main) is the primary production strategy, Cloud Run keeps immutable revisions so you can shift 100% of traffic back to a known-good revision in seconds: gcloud run revisions list \ --service=support-ops-agent \ --region="$DEPLOY_REGION" \ --project="$GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT" gcloud run services update-traffic support-ops-agent \ --to-revisions=REVISION_NAME=100 \ --region="$DEPLOY_REGION" \ --project="$GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT" Optional Cost Cleanup: Because agents-cli deploy sets --min-instances 0 by default, an idle service incurs zero compute cost (and keeping support-ops-agent live lets you register its A2A endpoint in Module 36!). Whenever you want to delete the Cloud Run service completely, run: gcloud run services delete support-ops-agent \ --region="$DEPLOY_REGION" \ --project="$GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT" \ --quiet

Built with Google ADK 2.0 (`gemini-3.8-flash`), stateful tools, and built-in A2A serving. """ from typing import Any, Dict from google.adk.agents import Agent from google.adk.agents.callback_context import CallbackContext from google.adk.apps import App from google.adk.models import Gemini from google.adk.tools.tool_context import ToolContext from google.genai import types MODEL = "gemini-3.8-flash" TICKET_DB: Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]] = { "TCK-1042": { "customer": "Acme Cloud Robotics", "tier": "enterprise", "severity": "P1", "status": "open", "summary": "Production payment webhook returning HTTP 503 timeouts in eu-west1.", }, "TCK-2088": { "customer": "Northwind Retail", "tier": "standard", "severity": "P3", "status": "investigating", "summary": "CSV invoice export omits localized tax column.", }, } SLA_POLICIES: Dict[str, Dict[str, str]] = { "enterprise": { "P1_response": "15 minutes", "P2_response": "1 hour", "P3_response": "4 hours", "dedicated_oncall": "Yes (24/7 SRE pager)", }, "standard": { "P1_response": "2 hours", "P2_response": "8 hours", "P3_response": "24 business hours", "dedicated_oncall": "No (business-hours queue)", }, } def initialize_support_state(callback_context: CallbackContext) -> None: """Initializes default session and user state keys before the first turn.""" if "user:customer_tier" not in callback_context.state: callback_context.state["user:customer_tier"] = "standard" if "escalated_tickets" not in callback_context.state: callback_context.state["escalated_tickets"] = [] def lookup_ticket(ticket_id: str, tool_context: ToolContext) -> Dict[str, Any]: """Looks up an enterprise support ticket by ID and syncs customer tier into state. Args: ticket_id: Ticket identifier such as 'TCK-1042' or 'TCK-2088'. """ norm_id = ticket_id.strip().upper() record = TICKET_DB.get(norm_id) if not record: return { "status": "not_found", "ticket_id": norm_id, "available_sample_tickets": sorted(TICKET_DB.keys()), "message": f"Ticket '{norm_id}' was not found.", } tool_context.state["user:customer_tier"] = record["tier"] tool_context.state["active_ticket_id"] = norm_id return {"status": "found", "ticket_id": norm_id, **record} def check_sla_policy(tier: str) -> Dict[str, Any]: """Returns response-time SLA targets for a customer tier ('enterprise' or 'standard'). Args: tier: Customer support tier ('enterprise' or 'standard'). """ norm_tier = tier.strip().lower() policy = SLA_POLICIES.get(norm_tier) if not policy: return { "status": "error", "message": f"Unknown tier '{tier}'. Valid tiers: enterprise, standard.", } return {"status": "success", "tier": norm_tier, "sla_targets": policy} def escalate_ticket( ticket_id: str, reason: str, tool_context: ToolContext, ) -> Dict[str, Any]: """Escalates a high-severity support ticket to the incident engineering queue. Args: ticket_id: Ticket identifier to escalate (e.g., 'TCK-1042'). reason: Concise technical justification for the escalation. """ norm_id = ticket_id.strip().upper() if norm_id not in TICKET_DB: return {"status": "error", "message": f"Cannot escalate unknown ticket '{norm_id}'."} escalated = list(tool_context.state.get("escalated_tickets", [])) if norm_id not in escalated: escalated.append(norm_id) tool_context.state["escalated_tickets"] = escalated tier = tool_context.state.get("user:customer_tier", TICKET_DB[norm_id]["tier"]) queue = "24/7 P1 SRE Oncall" if tier == "enterprise" else "Tier-2 Engineering Queue" return { "status": "escalated", "ticket_id": norm_id, "assigned_queue": queue, "reason": reason.strip(), "session_escalated_tickets": escalated, } # Keep name="support_ops_agent" in sync with root_agent_name in agents-cli-manifest.yaml root_agent = Agent( name="support_ops_agent", model=Gemini( model=MODEL, retry_options=types.HttpRetryOptions(attempts=3), ), before_agent_callback=initialize_support_state, instruction=( "You are the Support Operations Agent (active customer tier: {user:customer_tier?}).
" "Follow this exact operational workflow:
" "1. When given a ticket ID, ALWAYS call `lookup_ticket` first.
" "2. Call `check_sla_policy` for the ticket's customer tier so your answer cites exact SLA response times.
" "3. If a ticket has P1 severity OR the user requests escalation, call `escalate_ticket` with a concise technical reason.
" "4. Summarize the ticket status, applicable SLA target, and any escalation queue clearly." ), tools=[lookup_ticket, check_sla_policy, escalate_ticket], ) # CRITICAL for agents-cli: App `name` MUST match `agent_directory: "app"` in agents-cli-manifest.yaml app = App( root_agent=root_agent, name="app", ) Complete End-to-End Cloud Run Commands (Steps 1–4)​ # Step 1: Fast-bootstrap (if not reusing Module 31 directory) agents-cli scaffold create support-ops-agent --agent adk --prototype --agent-guidance-filename GEMINI.md curl -fsSL https://mauripsale.github.io/doc-adk-training/samples/part6/agent.py -o support-ops-agent/app/agent.py curl -fsSL https://mauripsale.github.io/doc-adk-training/samples/part6/basic-dataset.json -o support-ops-agent/tests/eval/datasets/basic-dataset.json cd support-ops-agent # Step 2: Enhance in place for Cloud Run export GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT=YOUR_PROJECT_ID export DEPLOY_REGION=us-central1 agents-cli scaffold enhance . \ --deployment-target cloud_run \ --cicd-runner github_actions \ --region "$DEPLOY_REGION" agents-cli install # Step 3: Dry-run preview & live deploy agents-cli deploy \ --project "$GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT" \ --region "$DEPLOY_REGION" \ --env-vars "GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_ENTERPRISE=1,GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION=global" \ --no-confirm-project \ --dry-run agents-cli deploy \ --project "$GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT" \ --region "$DEPLOY_REGION" \ --env-vars "GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_ENTERPRISE=1,GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION=global" \ --no-confirm-project # Step 4: Live A2A test, ADK SSE test, and remote evaluation SERVICE_URL=$(gcloud run services describe support-ops-agent \ --region="$DEPLOY_REGION" \ --project="$GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT" \ --format='value(status.url)') agents-cli run "Investigate ticket TCK-1042 and check SLA." --url "$SERVICE_URL" --mode a2a agents-cli run "Check ticket TCK-2088." --url "$SERVICE_URL" --mode adk --app-name app agents-cli eval generate --url "$SERVICE_URL" --app-name app && agents-cli eval grade Troubleshooting Common Cloud Run Errors​ 404 NOT_FOUND calling gemini-3.8-flash at runtime: Cause: GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION defaulted to us-central1 instead of global. Fix: Redeploy with --env-vars "GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_ENTERPRISE=1,GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION=global". 403 Forbidden when testing with raw curl: Cause: Cloud Run services deployed by agents-cli require IAM authentication (roles/run.invoker) by default. Fix: Test via agents-cli run --url "$SERVICE_URL" --mode a2a (which attaches credentials automatically) or pass -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-identity-token)" to curl. PERMISSION_DENIED on Cloud Build or Artifact Registry: Fix: Ensure run.googleapis.com, cloudbuild.googleapis.com, artifactregistry.googleapis.com, and aiplatform.googleapis.com are enabled and your account holds Editor/Owner or Cloud Run/Cloud Build admin roles. Inspecting container crash logs: Fix: Run gcloud logging read "resource.type=cloud_run_revision AND resource.labels.service_name=support-ops-agent" --project="$GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT" --limit=50 --format="table(timestamp,severity,textPayload)". Self-Reflection Answers​ Why does agents-cli deploy default to --no-allow-unauthenticated on Cloud Run, and how would you expose a browser-accessible internal tool safely to employees without writing custom login code? Answer: Leaving an LLM-backed endpoint unauthenticated on the public internet risks quota exhaustion (denial-of-wallet) and unauthorized tool execution. Requiring Cloud Run IAM authentication protects machine-to-machine callers, while passing agents-cli deploy --iap enables Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP) so authorized Google Workspace users can sign in through Google's zero-trust proxy with zero application auth code. If load testing with tests/load_test/load_test.py triggers container OOM restarts when you raise --concurrency from 8 to 32, which flag should you scale alongside --concurrency and why? Answer: Scale --memory (e.g., --memory 16Gi alongside --cpu 4 --concurrency 32). Because Uvicorn serves concurrent requests inside a single async Python process while awaiting Gemini responses, every in-flight request holds its conversation state, tool outputs, and streaming buffers in memory simultaneously. What happens to active conversation history in support-ops-agent when a Cloud Run instance scales down to zero under the default in_memory session configuration, and which scaffold enhance flag solves this for stateful production apps? Answer: With in_memory sessions, scaling to zero (or landing on a different container replica) loses prior session state. Passing --session-type cloud_sql (managed PostgreSQL 15 with IAM authentication) or --session-type agent_platform_sessions to agents-cli scaffold enhance persists sessions durably across container restarts and horizontal autoscaling.

Why does agents-cli deploy default to --no-allow-unauthenticated on Cloud Run, and how would you expose a browser-accessible internal tool safely to employees without writing custom login code? Answer: Leaving an LLM-backed endpoint unauthenticated on the public internet risks quota exhaustion (denial-of-wallet) and unauthorized tool execution. Requiring Cloud Run IAM authentication protects machine-to-machine callers, while passing agents-cli deploy --iap enables Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP) so authorized Google Workspace users can sign in through Google's zero-trust proxy with zero application auth code. If load testing with tests/load_test/load_test.py triggers container OOM restarts when you raise --concurrency from 8 to 32, which flag should you scale alongside --concurrency and why? Answer: Scale --memory (e.g., --memory 16Gi alongside --cpu 4 --concurrency 32). Because Uvicorn serves concurrent requests inside a single async Python process while awaiting Gemini responses, every in-flight request holds its conversation state, tool outputs, and streaming buffers in memory simultaneously. What happens to active conversation history in support-ops-agent when a Cloud Run instance scales down to zero under the default in_memory session configuration, and which scaffold enhance flag solves this for stateful production apps? Answer: With in_memory sessions, scaling to zero (or landing on a different container replica) loses prior session state. Passing --session-type cloud_sql (managed PostgreSQL 15 with IAM authentication) or --session-type agent_platform_sessions to agents-cli scaffold enhance persists sessions durably across container restarts and horizontal autoscaling.
Figure: Enterprise agent container orchestration on Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) with private VPC networking and multi-pod replica management.

In Module 32, you deployed an agent to Google Cloud Run — a serverless container platform that scales down to zero and abstracts away cluster management. For stateless or bursty HTTP agents, Cloud Run or Vertex AI Agent Runtime are ideal starting points. However, enterprise platform teams choose Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) when workloads demand deeper infrastructure control: Custom Compute & Accelerators: Running co-located GPU/TPU inference sidecars, custom compute classes, or memory-intensive pods alongside your ADK agent. Private Zero-Trust Networking: Enforcing Kubernetes NetworkPolicy rules, service meshes, internal VPC-only LoadBalancers for pod-to-pod A2A traffic, and custom Cloud NAT egress gateways. Sidecar Architectures: Pairing agent containers with dedicated proxy sidecars (such as the Cloud SQL Auth Proxy for persistent session state or OpenTelemetry collectors). Unified Platform Standardization: Operating agents inside an organization's existing Kubernetes GitOps, Prometheus, and fleet governance ecosystem.
documents.s: When You Need Full Cluster Control

documents.t: Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) Autopilot manages the Kubernetes control plane, node provisioning, and security hardening while preserving the full Kubernetes API (Deployment, Service, HorizontalPodAutoscaler, PodDisruptionBudget, and Workload Identity). Criteria Google Cloud Run GKE Autopilot (--deployment-target gke) Abstraction Level High (Serverless container revisions) Medium (Managed Kubernetes cluster & pods) Scaling Mechanism Revision concurrency + instance auto-scaling (including scale-to-zero) Declarative HorizontalPodAutoscaler (HPA), VPA, and node auto-provisioning Sizing Configuration Imperative agents-cli deploy flags (--cpu, --memory, --concurrency) or Terraform Declarative Terraform only (deployment/terraform/); CLI sizing flags are rejected Networking Public HTTPS URL with IAM auth (--no-allow-unauthenticated) or VPC egress Private VPC + Cloud NAT + Internal LoadBalancer by default (kubectl port-forward for dev) Persistent Sessions Cloud SQL via Unix socket volume mount or Agent Platform Sessions Cloud SQL via Auth Proxy sidecar container in the pod or Agent Platform Sessions Rollback Mechanism Cloud Run revision traffic shifting (gcloud run services update-traffic) Kubernetes rollout history (kubectl rollout undo deployment/...) or GitOps
documents.s: Cloud Run vs. GKE Autopilot: Architectural Trade-Offs

documents.t: Figure: Multi-tier GKE cluster topology showing load balancer ingress, replica Agent Pods governed by HPA and PDB, private VPC services, and Workload Identity. Hand-writing VPC subnets, Cloud NAT routers, Artifact Registry repositories, IAM bindings, and multi-object Kubernetes manifests from scratch is error-prone. agents-cli (google-agents-cli) codifies Google Cloud's production GKE Autopilot golden path into a repeatable scaffold-and-deploy workflow. Whether you create a new GKE project or upgrade an existing prototype (support-ops-agent) in place, agents-cli generates the complete container and Terraform stack automatically: export GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT="your-project-id" export DEPLOY_REGION="us-central1" # Option A: Create a new GKE-targeted ADK project with GitHub Actions CI/CD agents-cli scaffold create support-ops-gke \ --agent adk \ --deployment-target gke \ --cicd-runner github_actions \ --region "$DEPLOY_REGION" \ --agent-guidance-filename GEMINI.md # Option B: Upgrade an existing prototype directory in place # agents-cli scaffold enhance . --deployment-target gke --cicd-runner github_actions What agents-cli Automates Under deployment/terraform/​ When you select --deployment-target gke, agents-cli generates two Terraform layouts — deployment/terraform/single-project/ (for single-project environments and agents-cli deploy) and deployment/terraform/cicd/ (for staging/production CI/CD pipelines): GKE Autopilot & Private Networking (service.tf): Provisions a dedicated VPC, subnet, Cloud Router + Cloud NAT (so private Autopilot nodes can reach Vertex AI endpoints without public node IPs), Artifact Registry, and a GKE Autopilot cluster. Keyless Workload Identity (iam.tf & kubernetes_service_account_v1): Creates a least-privilege GCP runtime service account (app_sa) and binds it to the Kubernetes ServiceAccount via roles/iam.workloadIdentityUser. Pods authenticate to Vertex AI, Cloud Trace, and Secret Manager automatically — zero service account JSON keys are ever created or mounted. Declarative Kubernetes Workloads & Autoscaling (service.tf): kubernetes_deployment_v1: Runs your single-stage uv-built Dockerfile (uvicorn app.fast_api_app:app on port 8080, exposing both /run_sse and /a2a/app), configured with startup, readiness, and liveness probes, resource requests/limits, and an optional Cloud SQL Auth Proxy sidecar when --session-type cloud_sql is used. kubernetes_horizontal_pod_autoscaler_v2 (HPA): Automatically scales pod replicas (default 2 to 10 replicas at 70% CPU utilization). kubernetes_pod_disruption_budget_v1 (PDB): Enforces minAvailable: 1 so GKE node maintenance never takes all agent pods offline simultaneously. kubernetes_service_v1: Exposes port 8080 via an Internal LoadBalancer (cloud.google.com/load-balancer-type: "Internal") by default for private intra-VPC and A2A traffic. During development, you tunnel from your laptop with kubectl port-forward and test directly via agents-cli run --url ... --mode a2a or --mode adk. Critical agents-cli Rule for GKE Sizing: Unlike Cloud Run and Agent Runtime — where you can pass --cpu, --memory, --concurrency, --min-instances, --max-instances, or --service-name directly on agents-cli deploy — those sizing and naming flags are rejected on GKE. Why? Because on GKE, pod resource requests/limits, service names, and HorizontalPodAutoscaler bounds are owned declaratively in deployment/terraform/single-project/service.tf (and cicd/service.tf). Rejecting imperative CLI sizing flags prevents ad-hoc deployments from drifting out of sync with Terraform and HPA rules. When deploying gemini-3.8-flash to a regional GKE cluster (such as DEPLOY_REGION=us-central1), pass GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_ENTERPRISE=1 and GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION=global via --env-vars so the container routes model inference to the global Vertex AI endpoint: agents-cli deploy \ --project "$GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT" \ --region "$DEPLOY_REGION" \ --env-vars "GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_ENTERPRISE=1,GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION=global" \ --no-confirm-project

documents.t: While agents-cli automates cluster creation, Terraform state, and FastAPI/A2A packaging, understanding the raw Kubernetes primitives underneath makes you far more effective when debugging pod rollouts or customizing cluster topologies. When deploying an ADK agent manually without agents-cli, five core steps occur beneath the surface: Containerize with Headless adk api_server: Package your agent subdirectory inside /app/<agent_name>/ (containing __init__.py and agent.py) and run adk api_server /app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8080 — never adk web, which exposes debug traces and UI overhead in production. Build & Push to Artifact Registry: Submit the container build via Cloud Build (gcloud builds submit) to a regional Docker repository (${DEPLOY_REGION}-docker.pkg.dev/...). Provision GKE Autopilot: Create a cluster (gcloud container clusters create-auto) and fetch kubeconfig credentials (get-credentials). Author Kubernetes Manifests (deployment.yaml): A Deployment defines execution: which container image to pull, how many pod replicas to run, and container environment variables (GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_ENTERPRISE="1", GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION="global"). A Service defines network access: a stable IP address and load balancer routing traffic to ephemeral pod IPs selected by label (app: support-agent). Apply & Operate with kubectl: Apply manifests via kubectl apply -f, inspect logs via kubectl logs, and recover from bad image pushes instantaneously via kubectl rollout undo deployment/<name>. 🎯 Knowledge CheckSelect Best Answer When containerizing an ADK agent named 'support_agent' for GKE using 'adk api_server /app --port 8080', how must the agent files be structured inside '/app' so that HTTP requests to '/apps/support_agent/...' succeed instead of returning 404 Not Found? APlace 'agent.py' directly at the filesystem root '/' and omit '__init__.py'BPlace the agent package inside a subdirectory '/app/support_agent/' (containing '__init__.py' and 'agent.py') and pass the parent directory '/app' to 'adk api_server'CRename the Kubernetes Service to 'support_agent_service' with underscoresDRun 'adk web' instead of 'adk api_server' in production Check Answer 💡 Need a Hint?

documents.t: agents-cli Golden Path (--deployment-target gke): agents-cli scaffold create / enhance automates private VPC + Cloud NAT networking, GKE Autopilot cluster provisioning, Artifact Registry, keyless Workload Identity (app_sa), HorizontalPodAutoscaler (HPA), and PodDisruptionBudget (PDB) via deployment/terraform/. Declarative GKE Sizing Rule: Runtime sizing flags (--cpu, --memory, --concurrency, --min-instances, --max-instances) on agents-cli deploy are rejected for GKE because pod resource requests/limits and HPA scaling live declaratively in deployment/terraform/. Dual-Protocol Verification: Every agents-cli Python container serves uvicorn app.fast_api_app:app on port 8080, allowing you to test live GKE pods over both A2A (--mode a2a) and ADK SSE (--mode adk --app-name app) via agents-cli run --url. Deployment vs. Service Objects: Under the hood, a Kubernetes Deployment manages pod execution, replicas, and rolling updates (kubectl rollout undo), while a Service provides a stable network endpoint routing traffic across ephemeral pod IPs. adk api_server vs. adk web in Production: Always serve headless API containers (uvicorn app.fast_api_app:app in agents-cli or adk api_server in raw Dockerfiles) rather than adk web, which exposes internal instructions, tool schemas, and reasoning traces.

In this two-part lab, you will master deploying ADK 2.0 agents to Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) Autopilot from both the enterprise platform engineering perspective and the low-level Kubernetes perspective: Part 1 — Accelerated GKE Autopilot Deployment with agents-cli (Primary Golden Path): Scaffold support-ops-gke with --deployment-target gke, load the canonical Part 6 stateful support_ops_agent, inspect the generated Terraform modules (GKE Autopilot, Workload Identity app_sa, and HorizontalPodAutoscaler), deploy with agents-cli deploy, test the live endpoint over both A2A and ADK SSE via agents-cli run, and practice Kubernetes rollbacks. Part 2 — Under the Hood: Manual Dockerfile, deployment.yaml & kubectl Deep Dive: Build a raw container image running adk api_server /app and author Kubernetes Deployment and Service manifests manually to understand exactly what agents-cli orchestrates behind the scenes.

A Google Cloud Project with billing enabled. Google Cloud CLI (gcloud) installed and authenticated (gcloud auth login and gcloud auth application-default login). kubectl installed (gcloud components install kubectl) and terraform installed (>= 1.5). uv and google-agents-cli installed (uv tool install google-agents-cli). Environment setup: 1-Click Launch (Browser): Open in GitHub CodespacesOpen in Google Cloud Shell Local machine: If you're continuing the course in sequence, cd into the adk-training project you created in Module 2 and skip the block below -- your environment and dependencies already carry forward. If you're starting fresh at this module, create that project first: uv init adk-training --python 3.10 && cd adk-training uv add "google-adk>=2.1.0" python-dotenv DevContainer / Codespaces (Alternative): If you opened this repository in a DevContainer or GitHub Codespaces, Python 3.11, uv, gcloud, and all core ADK dependencies are pre-installed in your container environment.

Export your project ID and DEPLOY_REGION=us-central1 for regional GKE and Artifact Registry infrastructure, and enable the required Google Cloud APIs. Throughout both parts of this lab, we separate the cluster's regional location (us-central1) from the model inference endpoint (GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION=global) required by gemini-3.8-flash. export GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT=YOUR_PROJECT_ID export DEPLOY_REGION=us-central1 gcloud config set project "$GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT" gcloud services enable \ aiplatform.googleapis.com \ container.googleapis.com \ compute.googleapis.com \ artifactregistry.googleapis.com \ cloudbuild.googleapis.com \ iam.googleapis.com \ secretmanager.googleapis.com

Scaffold a GKE-targeted ADK project and load the canonical Part 6 agent: Run agents-cli scaffold create with --deployment-target gke (remember: do not mkdir support-ops-gke beforehand — agents-cli creates the directory), download the stateful support_ops_agent (lookup_ticket, check_sla_policy, escalate_ticket, and App(root_agent=root_agent, name="app")), and install dependencies: export GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT=YOUR_PROJECT_ID export DEPLOY_REGION=us-central1 agents-cli scaffold create support-ops-gke \ --agent adk \ --deployment-target gke \ --cicd-runner github_actions \ --region "$DEPLOY_REGION" \ --agent-guidance-filename GEMINI.md curl -fsSL https://mauripsale.github.io/doc-adk-training/samples/part6/agent.py -o support-ops-gke/app/agent.py cd support-ops-gke agents-cli install (Tip: If you already have an existing support-ops-agent prototype directory from an earlier Part 6 module and want to add GKE support in place, run agents-cli scaffold enhance . --deployment-target gke --cicd-runner github_actions from inside that project directory.) Verify app/agent.py Alignment with agents-cli-manifest.yaml: Open app/agent.py and confirm three essential contracts: MODEL = "gemini-3.8-flash" root_agent = Agent(name="support_ops_agent", ...) app = App(root_agent=root_agent, name="app") matching agent_directory: "app" in agents-cli-manifest.yaml.

documents.t: Before deploying, inspect the infrastructure-as-code files that agents-cli generated under deployment/terraform/: ls -la deployment/terraform/single-project/ Examine two key files in deployment/terraform/single-project/: iam.tf (Workload Identity): Inspect how app_sa (the runtime GCP Service Account) is granted Vertex AI / telemetry permissions and bound to the Kubernetes ServiceAccount via roles/iam.workloadIdentityUser. Pods authenticate as app_sa with zero exported JSON keys. service.tf (Cluster, Pod Sizing, HPA & Internal LB): Locate the private VPC/Cloud NAT resources, GKE Autopilot cluster, kubernetes_deployment_v1, kubernetes_horizontal_pod_autoscaler_v2 (2–10 replicas at 70% CPU), kubernetes_pod_disruption_budget_v1 (minAvailable: 1), and kubernetes_service_v1 (annotated as an internal LoadBalancer on port 8080). Why GKE Rejects CLI Sizing Flags: Try checking agents-cli deploy --help. Passing --cpu, --memory, or --concurrency to agents-cli deploy on a GKE project fails intentionally — pod resource requests/limits and HorizontalPodAutoscaler rules are managed declaratively in deployment/terraform/single-project/service.tf (and deployment/terraform/cicd/service.tf) so imperative CLI deploys never conflict with HPA or Terraform state.

documents.t: Preview the deployment plan first with --dry-run, then run agents-cli deploy (note that provisioning a new GKE Autopilot cluster on the first run takes roughly 8–12 minutes): # Preview what agents-cli will build and apply agents-cli deploy \ --project "$GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT" \ --region "$DEPLOY_REGION" \ --env-vars "GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_ENTERPRISE=1,GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION=global" \ --no-confirm-project \ --dry-run # Execute the build, push, and GKE Autopilot deployment agents-cli deploy \ --project "$GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT" \ --region "$DEPLOY_REGION" \ --env-vars "GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_ENTERPRISE=1,GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION=global" \ --no-confirm-project

documents.t: By default, agents-cli configures the GKE Service as an Internal LoadBalancer inside your private VPC so pod-to-pod A2A traffic is never exposed to the public internet. Forward port 8080 from the GKE service to your laptop (or point GKE_SERVICE_URL at your ingress endpoint), then verify both protocols with agents-cli run: # Fetch cluster credentials if not already configured in kubeconfig, then port-forward kubectl get svc -A kubectl port-forward svc/support-ops-gke 8080:8080 -n support-ops-gke & PF_PID=$! sleep 2 export GKE_SERVICE_URL="http://127.0.0.1:8080" # 1. Test over the built-in Agent-to-Agent (A2A) JSON-RPC protocol agents-cli run "Investigate ticket TCK-1042 and escalate if P1." --url "$GKE_SERVICE_URL" --mode a2a # 2. Test over the native ADK SSE streaming surface (/run_sse) agents-cli run "Check SLA for enterprise tier." --url "$GKE_SERVICE_URL" --mode adk --app-name app # Stop the background port-forward when finished kill "$PF_PID" Observe how the same GKE pod seamlessly serves A2A requests (discovering the agent card automatically and executing lookup_ticket → check_sla_policy → escalate_ticket for P1 ticket TCK-1042) as well as native ADK /run_sse sessions!

documents.t: In production, platform engineers inspect active deployments with agents-cli and recover instantaneously from faulty container releases using Kubernetes' native ReplicaSet history: # List deployments discovered in the project/region agents-cli deploy --list --project "$GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT" --region "$DEPLOY_REGION" # Inspect pod status and Deployment revision history kubectl get pods -n support-ops-gke kubectl rollout history deployment/support-ops-gke -n support-ops-gke # Roll back immediately to the previous healthy ReplicaSet revision (and monitor completion) kubectl rollout undo deployment/support-ops-gke -n support-ops-gke kubectl rollout status deployment/support-ops-gke -n support-ops-gke Return to your parent workspace directory before starting Part 2: cd ..

Define `billing_agent` (name="billing_agent", model="gemini-3.8-flash") # to politely handle questions about billing, invoices, and payments. billing_agent = None # TODO: 2. Define `tech_support_agent` (name="tech_support_agent", model="gemini-3.8-flash") # to troubleshoot technical issues and provide clear solutions. tech_support_agent = None # TODO: 3. Define `root_agent` (name="router_agent", model="gemini-3.8-flash") # that delegates billing questions to `billing_agent` and technical problems # to `tech_support_agent` via `sub_agents=[billing_agent, tech_support_agent]`. root_agent = None

documents.t: Create requirements.txt: echo "google-adk" > requirements.txt Create Dockerfile in gke_support_agent/: Notice how support_agent/ is copied into /app/support_agent/ while /app is passed as AGENTS_DIR to adk api_server. Copying files flat into /app would mount routes at /apps/app/... instead of /apps/support_agent/...! FROM python:3.11-slim WORKDIR /app COPY requirements.txt . RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt COPY support_agent/ /app/support_agent/ EXPOSE 8080 CMD ["adk", "api_server", "/app", "--host", "0.0.0.0", "--port", "8080"]
