Here is the official reference walkthrough and architecture review: 🎉 Challenge Lab Unlocked! Record this lab as completed in your study plan? ✓ Mark as Complete Lab 33 Solution: Deploying Enterprise Agents to GKE Autopilot Goal​ This solution provides the complete runnable Python code for Part 1 (support-ops-gke/app/agent.py deployed via agents-cli --deployment-target gke) and Part 2 (gke_support_agent/support_agent/ deployed manually via Dockerfile + deployment.yaml + kubectl), along with expected outputs and troubleshooting guidance. Part 1 Solution: support-ops-gke/app/agent.py (agents-cli Golden Path)​ """ Enterprise Support Operations Agent — Canonical Part 6 End-to-End Agent (`agents-cli`). Built with Google ADK 2.0 (`gemini-3.8-flash`), stateful tools, and built-in A2A serving. """ from typing import Any, Dict from google.adk.agents import Agent from google.adk.agents.callback_context import CallbackContext from google.adk.apps import App from google.adk.models import Gemini from google.adk.tools.tool_context import ToolContext from google.genai import types MODEL = "gemini-3.8-flash" TICKET_DB: Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]] = { "TCK-1042": { "customer": "Acme Cloud Robotics", "tier": "enterprise", "severity": "P1", "status": "open", "summary": "Production payment webhook returning HTTP 503 timeouts in eu-west1.", }, "TCK-2088": { "customer": "Northwind Retail", "tier": "standard", "severity": "P3", "status": "investigating", "summary": "CSV invoice export omits localized tax column.", }, } SLA_POLICIES: Dict[str, Dict[str, str]] = { "enterprise": { "P1_response": "15 minutes", "P2_response": "1 hour", "P3_response": "4 hours", "dedicated_oncall": "Yes (24/7 SRE pager)", }, "standard": { "P1_response": "2 hours", "P2_response": "8 hours", "P3_response": "24 business hours", "dedicated_oncall": "No (business-hours queue)", }, } def initialize_support_state(callback_context: CallbackContext) -> None: """Initializes default session and user state keys before the first turn.""" if "user:customer_tier" not in callback_context.state: callback_context.state["user:customer_tier"] = "standard" if "escalated_tickets" not in callback_context.state: callback_context.state["escalated_tickets"] = [] def lookup_ticket(ticket_id: str, tool_context: ToolContext) -> Dict[str, Any]: """Looks up an enterprise support ticket by ID and syncs customer tier into state. Args: ticket_id: Ticket identifier such as 'TCK-1042' or 'TCK-2088'. """ norm_id = ticket_id.strip().upper() record = TICKET_DB.get(norm_id) if not record: return { "status": "not_found", "ticket_id": norm_id, "available_sample_tickets": sorted(TICKET_DB.keys()), "message": f"Ticket '{norm_id}' was not found.", } tool_context.state["user:customer_tier"] = record["tier"] tool_context.state["active_ticket_id"] = norm_id return {"status": "found", "ticket_id": norm_id, **record} def check_sla_policy(tier: str) -> Dict[str, Any]: """Returns response-time SLA targets for a customer tier ('enterprise' or 'standard'). Args: tier: Customer support tier ('enterprise' or 'standard'). """ norm_tier = tier.strip().lower() policy = SLA_POLICIES.get(norm_tier) if not policy: return { "status": "error", "message": f"Unknown tier '{tier}'. Valid tiers: enterprise, standard.", } return {"status": "success", "tier": norm_tier, "sla_targets": policy} def escalate_ticket( ticket_id: str, reason: str, tool_context: ToolContext, ) -> Dict[str, Any]: """Escalates a high-severity support ticket to the incident engineering queue. Args: ticket_id: Ticket identifier to escalate (e.g., 'TCK-1042'). reason: Concise technical justification for the escalation. """ norm_id = ticket_id.strip().upper() if norm_id not in TICKET_DB: return {"status": "error", "message": f"Cannot escalate unknown ticket '{norm_id}'."} escalated = list(tool_context.state.get("escalated_tickets", [])) if norm_id not in escalated: escalated.append(norm_id) tool_context.state["escalated_tickets"] = escalated tier = tool_context.state.get("user:customer_tier", TICKET_DB[norm_id]["tier"]) queue = "24/7 P1 SRE Oncall" if tier == "enterprise" else "Tier-2 Engineering Queue" return { "status": "escalated", "ticket_id": norm_id, "assigned_queue": queue, "reason": reason.strip(), "session_escalated_tickets": escalated, } # Keep name="support_ops_agent" in sync with root_agent_name in agents-cli-manifest.yaml root_agent = Agent( name="support_ops_agent", model=Gemini( model=MODEL, retry_options=types.HttpRetryOptions(attempts=3), ), before_agent_callback=initialize_support_state, instruction=( "You are the Support Operations Agent (active customer tier: {user:customer_tier?}).
" "Follow this exact operational workflow:
" "1. When given a ticket ID, ALWAYS call `lookup_ticket` first.
" "2. Call `check_sla_policy` for the ticket's customer tier so your answer cites exact SLA response times.
" "3. If a ticket has P1 severity OR the user requests escalation, call `escalate_ticket` with a concise technical reason.
" "4. Summarize the ticket status, applicable SLA target, and any escalation queue clearly." ), tools=[lookup_ticket, check_sla_policy, escalate_ticket], ) # CRITICAL for agents-cli: App `name` MUST match `agent_directory: "app"` in agents-cli-manifest.yaml app = App( root_agent=root_agent, name="app", ) Part 2 Solution: Raw Manual GKE Package (gke_support_agent/)​ support_agent/__init__.py​ from . import agent support_agent/agent.py​ from google.adk.agents import Agent billing_agent = Agent( name="billing_agent", model="gemini-3.8-flash", description="Handles questions about billing, invoices, and payments.", instruction="You are a billing support agent. Politely answer questions about billing and payment issues.", ) tech_support_agent = Agent( name="tech_support_agent", model="gemini-3.8-flash", description="Handles technical support questions and troubleshooting.", instruction="You are a technical support agent. Help users troubleshoot technical issues and provide clear solutions.", ) root_agent = Agent( name="router_agent", model="gemini-3.8-flash", description="The main customer support router.", instruction=""" You are the customer support router. Your job is to understand the user's request and delegate it to the correct specialist agent. - If the user has a question about billing, delegate to the `billing_agent`. - If the user has a technical problem, delegate to the `tech_support_agent`. """, sub_agents=[billing_agent, tech_support_agent], ) Dockerfile​ FROM python:3.11-slim WORKDIR /app COPY requirements.txt . RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt COPY support_agent/ /app/support_agent/ EXPOSE 8080 CMD ["adk", "api_server", "/app", "--host", "0.0.0.0", "--port", "8080"] Expected Outputs​ Part 1: agents-cli run Against Live GKE Service​ A2A Mode (--mode a2a): Resolves the agent card from /a2a/app, invokes lookup_ticket("TCK-1042"), check_sla_policy("enterprise"), and escalate_ticket("TCK-1042", ...), and reports the 15 minutes P1 SLA target and 24/7 P1 SRE Oncall escalation queue. ADK SSE Mode (--mode adk --app-name app): Creates an ADK session under /apps/app/..., streams SSE events from /run_sse, and returns the enterprise SLA policy targets (15 minutes P1, 1 hour P2, 4 hours P3). Part 2: kubectl apply & kubectl get service --watch​ deployment.apps/support-agent-deployment created service/support-agent-service created NAME TYPE CLUSTER-IP EXTERNAL-IP PORT(S) AGE support-agent-service LoadBalancer 10.44.192.123 34.123.45.67 80:30123/TCP 2m30s Troubleshooting Common GKE Errors​ Passing --cpu / --memory / --concurrency on agents-cli deploy fails: Cause: agents-cli rejects imperative container sizing flags for GKE targets. Solution: Edit pod resource requests/limits and kubernetes_horizontal_pod_autoscaler_v2 settings declaratively in deployment/terraform/single-project/service.tf (and cicd/service.tf). kubectl apply fails with metadata.name: Invalid value ... RFC 1123 label: Cause: Kubernetes resource names cannot contain underscores (_), even when your Python package (support_agent) uses underscores. Solution: Always use hyphens (support-agent-deployment, support-agent-service) in Kubernetes metadata.name fields. CrashLoopBackOff or 404 NOT_FOUND on gemini-3.8-flash: Cause: Missing GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_ENTERPRISE=1 or GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION=global in the pod environment, or mismatched AGENTS_DIR inside Dockerfile. Solution: Inspect pod logs with kubectl logs deployment/<deployment-name> and ensure GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_ENTERPRISE="1" and GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION="global" are set. Self-Reflection Answers​ Why does agents-cli deploy reject --cpu, --memory, and --concurrency flags when --deployment-target gke is configured, whereas Cloud Run and Agent Runtime accept them? Answer: On GKE, pod resource requests/limits and replica scaling (HorizontalPodAutoscaler + PodDisruptionBudget) are governed declaratively by Kubernetes resources inside deployment/terraform/. Allowing ad-hoc CLI sizing flags during image deployment would create configuration drift between live Kubernetes cluster state and Terraform IaC, and could conflict with HPA target utilization metrics. How does GKE Workload Identity (app_sa in iam.tf) eliminate the security risks of static service account JSON keys? Answer: Workload Identity binds a Kubernetes ServiceAccount directly to a GCP IAM Service Account (app_sa) using roles/iam.workloadIdentityUser. GKE's metadata server automatically issues short-lived, auto-rotating OAuth credentials to pods running under that Kubernetes ServiceAccount, completely eliminating downloadable JSON key files that could be leaked or committed to Git. In Part 2's deployment.yaml, what is the distinct role of the Deployment object versus the Service object, and why is adk api_server used in the Dockerfile instead of adk web? Answer: The Deployment manages pod execution, desired replica counts, self-healing, and rolling updates/rollbacks, whereas the Service provides a stable IP and load balancer across ephemeral pod IPs. adk api_server exposes a lean, headless REST/SSE API suitable for production backends, whereas adk web bundles the developer debug UI — exposing internal agent prompts, tool definitions, and execution traces while consuming extra memory and CPU.
Locked Challenge — Active Pedagogical Socratic Gate

This solution provides the complete runnable Python code for Part 1 (support-ops-gke/app/agent.py deployed via agents-cli --deployment-target gke) and Part 2 (gke_support_agent/support_agent/ deployed manually via Dockerfile + deployment.yaml + kubectl), along with expected outputs and troubleshooting guidance.

""" Enterprise Support Operations Agent — Canonical Part 6 End-to-End Agent (`agents-cli`). Built with Google ADK 2.0 (`gemini-3.8-flash`), stateful tools, and built-in A2A serving. """ from typing import Any, Dict from google.adk.agents import Agent from google.adk.agents.callback_context import CallbackContext from google.adk.apps import App from google.adk.models import Gemini from google.adk.tools.tool_context import ToolContext from google.genai import types MODEL = "gemini-3.8-flash" TICKET_DB: Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]] = { "TCK-1042": { "customer": "Acme Cloud Robotics", "tier": "enterprise", "severity": "P1", "status": "open", "summary": "Production payment webhook returning HTTP 503 timeouts in eu-west1.", }, "TCK-2088": { "customer": "Northwind Retail", "tier": "standard", "severity": "P3", "status": "investigating", "summary": "CSV invoice export omits localized tax column.", }, } SLA_POLICIES: Dict[str, Dict[str, str]] = { "enterprise": { "P1_response": "15 minutes", "P2_response": "1 hour", "P3_response": "4 hours", "dedicated_oncall": "Yes (24/7 SRE pager)", }, "standard": { "P1_response": "2 hours", "P2_response": "8 hours", "P3_response": "24 business hours", "dedicated_oncall": "No (business-hours queue)", }, } def initialize_support_state(callback_context: CallbackContext) -> None: """Initializes default session and user state keys before the first turn.""" if "user:customer_tier" not in callback_context.state: callback_context.state["user:customer_tier"] = "standard" if "escalated_tickets" not in callback_context.state: callback_context.state["escalated_tickets"] = [] def lookup_ticket(ticket_id: str, tool_context: ToolContext) -> Dict[str, Any]: """Looks up an enterprise support ticket by ID and syncs customer tier into state. Args: ticket_id: Ticket identifier such as 'TCK-1042' or 'TCK-2088'. """ norm_id = ticket_id.strip().upper() record = TICKET_DB.get(norm_id) if not record: return { "status": "not_found", "ticket_id": norm_id, "available_sample_tickets": sorted(TICKET_DB.keys()), "message": f"Ticket '{norm_id}' was not found.", } tool_context.state["user:customer_tier"] = record["tier"] tool_context.state["active_ticket_id"] = norm_id return {"status": "found", "ticket_id": norm_id, **record} def check_sla_policy(tier: str) -> Dict[str, Any]: """Returns response-time SLA targets for a customer tier ('enterprise' or 'standard'). Args: tier: Customer support tier ('enterprise' or 'standard'). """ norm_tier = tier.strip().lower() policy = SLA_POLICIES.get(norm_tier) if not policy: return { "status": "error", "message": f"Unknown tier '{tier}'. Valid tiers: enterprise, standard.", } return {"status": "success", "tier": norm_tier, "sla_targets": policy} def escalate_ticket( ticket_id: str, reason: str, tool_context: ToolContext, ) -> Dict[str, Any]: """Escalates a high-severity support ticket to the incident engineering queue. Args: ticket_id: Ticket identifier to escalate (e.g., 'TCK-1042'). reason: Concise technical justification for the escalation. """ norm_id = ticket_id.strip().upper() if norm_id not in TICKET_DB: return {"status": "error", "message": f"Cannot escalate unknown ticket '{norm_id}'."} escalated = list(tool_context.state.get("escalated_tickets", [])) if norm_id not in escalated: escalated.append(norm_id) tool_context.state["escalated_tickets"] = escalated tier = tool_context.state.get("user:customer_tier", TICKET_DB[norm_id]["tier"]) queue = "24/7 P1 SRE Oncall" if tier == "enterprise" else "Tier-2 Engineering Queue" return { "status": "escalated", "ticket_id": norm_id, "assigned_queue": queue, "reason": reason.strip(), "session_escalated_tickets": escalated, } # Keep name="support_ops_agent" in sync with root_agent_name in agents-cli-manifest.yaml root_agent = Agent( name="support_ops_agent", model=Gemini( model=MODEL, retry_options=types.HttpRetryOptions(attempts=3), ), before_agent_callback=initialize_support_state, instruction=( "You are the Support Operations Agent (active customer tier: {user:customer_tier?}).
" "Follow this exact operational workflow:
" "1. When given a ticket ID, ALWAYS call `lookup_ticket` first.
" "2. Call `check_sla_policy` for the ticket's customer tier so your answer cites exact SLA response times.
" "3. If a ticket has P1 severity OR the user requests escalation, call `escalate_ticket` with a concise technical reason.
" "4. Summarize the ticket status, applicable SLA target, and any escalation queue clearly." ), tools=[lookup_ticket, check_sla_policy, escalate_ticket], ) # CRITICAL for agents-cli: App `name` MUST match `agent_directory: "app"` in agents-cli-manifest.yaml app = App( root_agent=root_agent, name="app", )

support_agent/__init__.py​ from . import agent support_agent/agent.py​ from google.adk.agents import Agent billing_agent = Agent( name="billing_agent", model="gemini-3.8-flash", description="Handles questions about billing, invoices, and payments.", instruction="You are a billing support agent. Politely answer questions about billing and payment issues.", ) tech_support_agent = Agent( name="tech_support_agent", model="gemini-3.8-flash", description="Handles technical support questions and troubleshooting.", instruction="You are a technical support agent. Help users troubleshoot technical issues and provide clear solutions.", ) root_agent = Agent( name="router_agent", model="gemini-3.8-flash", description="The main customer support router.", instruction=""" You are the customer support router. Your job is to understand the user's request and delegate it to the correct specialist agent. - If the user has a question about billing, delegate to the `billing_agent`. - If the user has a technical problem, delegate to the `tech_support_agent`. """, sub_agents=[billing_agent, tech_support_agent], ) Dockerfile​ FROM python:3.11-slim WORKDIR /app COPY requirements.txt . RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt COPY support_agent/ /app/support_agent/ EXPOSE 8080 CMD ["adk", "api_server", "/app", "--host", "0.0.0.0", "--port", "8080"]

ADK SSE Mode (--mode adk --app-name app): Creates an ADK session under /apps/app/..., streams SSE events from /run_sse, and returns the enterprise SLA policy targets (15 minutes P1, 1 hour P2, 4 hours P3). Part 2: kubectl apply & kubectl get service --watch​ deployment.apps/support-agent-deployment created service/support-agent-service created NAME TYPE CLUSTER-IP EXTERNAL-IP PORT(S) AGE support-agent-service LoadBalancer 10.44.192.123 34.123.45.67 80:30123/TCP 2m30s

Passing --cpu / --memory / --concurrency on agents-cli deploy fails: Cause: agents-cli rejects imperative container sizing flags for GKE targets. Solution: Edit pod resource requests/limits and kubernetes_horizontal_pod_autoscaler_v2 settings declaratively in deployment/terraform/single-project/service.tf (and cicd/service.tf). kubectl apply fails with metadata.name: Invalid value ... RFC 1123 label: Cause: Kubernetes resource names cannot contain underscores (_), even when your Python package (support_agent) uses underscores. Solution: Always use hyphens (support-agent-deployment, support-agent-service) in Kubernetes metadata.name fields. CrashLoopBackOff or 404 NOT_FOUND on gemini-3.8-flash: Cause: Missing GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_ENTERPRISE=1 or GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION=global in the pod environment, or mismatched AGENTS_DIR inside Dockerfile. Solution: Inspect pod logs with kubectl logs deployment/<deployment-name> and ensure GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_ENTERPRISE="1" and GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION="global" are set.

Why does agents-cli deploy reject --cpu, --memory, and --concurrency flags when --deployment-target gke is configured, whereas Cloud Run and Agent Runtime accept them? Answer: On GKE, pod resource requests/limits and replica scaling (HorizontalPodAutoscaler + PodDisruptionBudget) are governed declaratively by Kubernetes resources inside deployment/terraform/. Allowing ad-hoc CLI sizing flags during image deployment would create configuration drift between live Kubernetes cluster state and Terraform IaC, and could conflict with HPA target utilization metrics. How does GKE Workload Identity (app_sa in iam.tf) eliminate the security risks of static service account JSON keys? Answer: Workload Identity binds a Kubernetes ServiceAccount directly to a GCP IAM Service Account (app_sa) using roles/iam.workloadIdentityUser. GKE's metadata server automatically issues short-lived, auto-rotating OAuth credentials to pods running under that Kubernetes ServiceAccount, completely eliminating downloadable JSON key files that could be leaked or committed to Git. In Part 2's deployment.yaml, what is the distinct role of the Deployment object versus the Service object, and why is adk api_server used in the Dockerfile instead of adk web? Answer: The Deployment manages pod execution, desired replica counts, self-healing, and rolling updates/rollbacks, whereas the Service provides a stable IP and load balancer across ephemeral pod IPs. adk api_server exposes a lean, headless REST/SSE API suitable for production backends, whereas adk web bundles the developer debug UI — exposing internal agent prompts, tool definitions, and execution traces while consuming extra memory and CPU.
Figure: Deploying stateless serverless MCP servers on Cloud Run backed by externalized distributed cache and database stores.

In Module 28, you built a stateful MCP server. Its state—the contents of the shopping cart—was a single global Python list: CART = []. That worked fine because the server ran over stdio, talking to exactly one client (your local agent) at a time — there was no notion of "whose cart is this" because there was only ever one. Moving to Cloud Run over HTTP changes that completely: the server can now be talking to many clients concurrently, each of whom needs their own, isolated cart. A single global list would mean every user shares the exact same cart — a correctness bug, not just a scaling one. And even setting that aside, Cloud Run is a stateless and serverless environment, which introduces a second problem on top of the first: Stateless: Each incoming request could be handled by a completely different container instance. An instance that handles a user's "add item" request might be shut down before the user makes a "view cart" request, which would then be routed to a brand new instance with no memory of the previous one. The in-memory cart data would be lost. Serverless: You don't have a single, persistent "server." Cloud Run automatically starts and stops container instances based on traffic. It might run ten instances to handle a spike in traffic and then scale down to zero when idle. If we deploy our simple, in-memory MCP server directly to Cloud Run, every user's shopping cart would be wiped out between requests. We need a new architecture.
documents.s: The Challenge of State in a Serverless World

documents.t: The solution to this challenge is to externalize the state. Instead of storing the session data in the memory of the MCP server process, the server must save it to and load it from an external, persistent storage service that all of its instances can access. This is a fundamental pattern in cloud-native application design. The application instances themselves remain stateless, which makes them easy to scale and replace, while the important data lives in a durable, centralized location. Common choices for an external state store include: In-memory caches: Services like Redis or Google Cloud Memorystore. These are extremely fast and are a perfect fit for session data that needs to be accessed quickly but may not need to be stored forever. Databases: Services like Firestore, DynamoDB, or a traditional SQL database like Cloud SQL. These are better for data that needs to be stored permanently and queried in more complex ways.

Figure: Request lifecycle showing Agent HTTP request, Cloud Run auto-routing, Redis/Firestore state sync, and stateless response dispatch. With externalized state, the interaction flow for our MCP server on Cloud Run looks like this: An ADK agent (the client) sends a call_tool request (e.g., add_item_to_cart) to the Cloud Run service URL. Cloud Run starts or selects a container instance to handle the request. The MCP server code inside the container reads the Mcp-Session-Id HTTP header that the MCP transport itself tracks for the connection. Instead of appending to a global in-memory list, the server connects to the external state store (e.g., Redis), keyed by that session ID. It retrieves the shopping cart for the given session, performs the action (adds the new item), and saves the updated cart back to the external store. It sends the success response back to the ADK agent. Now, if another request for the same session_id arrives a moment later, Cloud Run can send it to a completely different container instance. This new instance will follow the same process, connect to the same external store, and retrieve the correct, up-to-date shopping cart. The state is preserved.

When an MCP server runs on Cloud Run over HTTP, your ADK agent replaces local StdioConnectionParams with a network transport parameter class from google.adk.tools.mcp_tool: StreamableHTTPConnectionParams (Recommended): Connects over the modern MCP Streamable HTTP transport (mounted at /mcp by default in FastMCP), with optional headers (for Bearer tokens or API keys) and configurable timeouts. SseConnectionParams (Legacy HTTP+SSE): Connects to older MCP servers that expose a separate Server-Sent Events endpoint. Because McpToolset is a standard ADK toolset, the exact same wiring works both in standalone ADK packages (uv run adk web) and inside enterprise agents-cli projects (support-ops-agent/app/agent.py): import os from google.adk.tools.mcp_tool import McpToolset, StreamableHTTPConnectionParams MCP_SERVER_URL = os.environ.get("MCP_SERVER_URL", "https://mcp-cart-server-xyz.a.run.app").rstrip("/") MCP_AUTH_TOKEN = os.environ.get("MCP_AUTH_TOKEN", "") mcp_headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {MCP_AUTH_TOKEN}"} if MCP_AUTH_TOKEN else None remote_mcp_toolset = McpToolset( connection_params=StreamableHTTPConnectionParams( url=f"{MCP_SERVER_URL}/mcp", headers=mcp_headers, ) ) Inside an agents-cli project, once remote_mcp_toolset is added to root_agent.tools in app/agent.py (with app = App(root_agent=root_agent, name="app") preserved), you can smoke-test remote Cloud Run MCP tool execution immediately from your terminal or browser before redeploying: # Rapid CLI smoke test (with --start-server + --session-id to verify multi-turn MCP state) agents-cli run "Add 'p1-incident-runbook' to my cart and inspect ticket TCK-1042." \ --start-server --session-id ops-1 # Interactive web playground agents-cli playground
documents.s: Connecting Standalone ADK Agents and agents-cli Projects

documents.t: When deploying MCP servers to production, security and safety become paramount. The ADK provides advanced features to handle these requirements. Authentication​ You must secure your MCP server (for example, deploying Cloud Run with --no-allow-unauthenticated or behind an API gateway) so only authorized agents can invoke its tools. McpToolset and StreamableHTTPConnectionParams support multiple authentication patterns: OAuth2 (auth_scheme + auth_credential): Standard method for user-delegated or service-to-service production flows. ADK manages token acquisition and refresh automatically. HTTP Bearer / Cloud Run Identity Tokens (headers or header_provider): Pass static headers via StreamableHTTPConnectionParams(url=..., headers={"Authorization": "Bearer ..."}) or per-request dynamic tokens via McpToolset(..., header_provider=...). API Keys & HTTP Basic Auth: Supported via auth_scheme / auth_credential or custom HTTP headers. Human-in-the-Loop (HITL)​ When an MCP server provides powerful or destructive tools (e.g., write_file, delete_database_entry), it's crucial to have a human approval step to prevent accidental data loss or misuse. You can enforce HITL in ADK either via McpToolset(..., require_confirmation=True) or by implementing a before_tool_callback on your Agent: Check if the tool being called is on a list of high-impact or destructive operations. Block or pause execution and prompt for explicit human approval before allowing the remote MCP call to proceed. 🎯 Knowledge CheckSelect Best Answer Why must a stateful MCP server externalize its session data (for example, to Memorystore/Redis or Firestore) before being deployed to Cloud Run, and which ADK connection class connects to FastMCP's '/mcp' HTTP endpoint? ACloud Run instances are stateless and ephemeral—requests may hit different containers or scale to zero—and the client connects via 'StreamableHTTPConnectionParams'BCloud Run blocks all outbound database connections and requires 'StdioConnectionParams' over SSHCGlobal Python lists automatically replicate across all Cloud Run instances when 'SseConnectionParams' is usedDFastMCP automatically persists '/tmp' files across container termination without an external store Check Answer 💡 Need a Hint?

Serverless platforms like Cloud Run are stateless, meaning in-memory state is lost across horizontal scaling and scale-to-zero events. To deploy a stateful MCP server to Cloud Run, externalize session state (keyed by Mcp-Session-Id) into a shared backing store like Memorystore (Redis), Firestore, or Cloud SQL. Connect both standalone ADK agents (uv run adk web) and enterprise agents-cli projects (support-ops-agent/app/agent.py) to remote FastMCP servers using McpToolset(connection_params=StreamableHTTPConnectionParams(url=f"{MCP_SERVER_URL}/mcp", headers=...)), verifying behavior rapidly with agents-cli run and agents-cli playground. Separation of Concerns in MCP: Because McpToolset only depends on the remote /mcp URL and tool schemas, you can upgrade the MCP server's persistence layer from a /tmp demo store to Redis or Firestore without changing a single line of agent code. Persistence Caveat for /tmp: Container /tmp storage lives in volatile memory on Cloud Run and disappears whenever an instance is recycled or scales down to zero — always use a managed external store in production.

In this lab, you will take the stateful MCP server pattern from Module 28, re-architect it into a stateless FastMCP HTTP server, containerize it with a Dockerfile, and deploy it to Google Cloud Run. Then, in Steps 4 and 5, you will connect to your live Cloud Run /mcp endpoint in two ways: Standalone ADK Package (cloud_mcp_server/agent.py): Launch uv run adk web from the parent adk-training/ directory to test the remote MCP server interactively. Enterprise agents-cli Project (support-ops-agent/app/agent.py): Equip the canonical Part 6 support_ops_agent with McpToolset(connection_params=StreamableHTTPConnectionParams(url=f"{MCP_SERVER_URL}/mcp", headers=...)) and test it immediately via agents-cli run and agents-cli playground. Note: For lab simplicity, our server simulates externalized state using per-session JSON files in /tmp/carts keyed by the Mcp-Session-Id HTTP header. In production, you replace those two helper functions (get_cart / save_cart) with Google Cloud Memorystore (Redis) or Firestore.

A Google Cloud Project with billing enabled. Google Cloud CLI (gcloud) installed and authenticated. uv and google-agents-cli installed (uv tool install google-agents-cli). Required APIs: Cloud Run, Cloud Build, Artifact Registry, and Vertex AI: export GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT=YOUR_PROJECT_ID export DEPLOY_REGION=us-central1 gcloud config set project "$GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT" gcloud services enable run.googleapis.com cloudbuild.googleapis.com artifactregistry.googleapis.com aiplatform.googleapis.com

Environment setup: 1-Click Launch (Browser): Open in GitHub CodespacesOpen in Google Cloud Shell Local machine: If you're continuing the course in sequence, cd into the adk-training project you created in Module 2 and skip the block below -- your environment and dependencies already carry forward. If you're starting fresh at this module, create that project first: uv init adk-training --python 3.10 && cd adk-training uv add "google-adk>=2.1.0" python-dotenv DevContainer / Codespaces (Alternative): If you opened this repository in a DevContainer or GitHub Codespaces, Python 3.11, uv, gcloud, and all core ADK dependencies are pre-installed in your container environment. Create a new cloud_mcp_server directory inside your adk-training workspace: cd /path/to/your/adk-training mkdir cloud_mcp_server cd cloud_mcp_server Create stateless_cart_server.py: Using mcp.server.fastmcp.FastMCP, each tool call extracts the mcp-session-id HTTP header managed by the Streamable HTTP transport and reads/writes that session's isolated cart outside Python process globals: # Filename: stateless_cart_server.py import json import os from mcp.server.fastmcp import FastMCP, Context # --- Configuration --- # In a serverless environment, we use /tmp/carts to simulate an external store. # In production, replace get_cart/save_cart with Memorystore (Redis) or Firestore. STATE_STORAGE_PATH = "/tmp/carts" if not os.path.exists(STATE_STORAGE_PATH): os.makedirs(STATE_STORAGE_PATH) # --- MCP Server Setup --- mcp = FastMCP("stateless_shopping_cart_server") def get_session_id(ctx: Context) -> str: # The MCP session ID arrives as a standard HTTP header tracked by the transport. return ctx.request_context.request.headers.get("mcp-session-id", "unknown") def get_cart(session_id: str) -> list: cart_file = os.path.join(STATE_STORAGE_PATH, f"{session_id}.json") if os.path.exists(cart_file): with open(cart_file, "r") as f: return json.load(f) return [] def save_cart(session_id: str, cart: list) -> None: cart_file = os.path.join(STATE_STORAGE_PATH, f"{session_id}.json") with open(cart_file, "w") as f: json.dump(cart, f) @mcp.tool() def add_item_to_cart(item: str, ctx: Context) -> dict: """Adds an item to the session cart.""" session_id = get_session_id(ctx) print(f"[Server]: Handling add_item_to_cart for session '{session_id}'") cart = get_cart(session_id) cart.append(item) save_cart(session_id, cart) return {"status": "success", "message": f"Added '{item}'."} @mcp.tool() def view_cart(ctx: Context) -> dict: """Views all items currently in the session cart.""" session_id = get_session_id(ctx) print(f"[Server]: Handling view_cart for session '{session_id}'") cart = get_cart(session_id) return {"status": "success", "cart": cart} # --- ASGI app for HTTP, suitable for Cloud Run --- # FastMCP mounts the Streamable HTTP MCP endpoint at /mcp by default. app = mcp.streamable_http_app()

documents.t: Create requirements.txt: Pin mcp<2 alongside uvicorn so mcp.server.fastmcp.FastMCP and google-adk's McpToolset client stay aligned on the 1.x MCP SDK surface: printf "mcp<2\nuvicorn\n" > requirements.txt Create Dockerfile: FROM python:3.11-slim WORKDIR /app COPY requirements.txt . RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt COPY stateless_cart_server.py . # Cloud Run injects PORT (defaults to 8080 locally). # Shell form is used so ${PORT:-8080} expands at container startup. CMD python -m uvicorn stateless_cart_server:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port ${PORT:-8080}

STATE_STORAGE_PATH = "/tmp/carts" if not os.path.exists(STATE_STORAGE_PATH): os.makedirs(STATE_STORAGE_PATH) # --- MCP Server Setup --- mcp = FastMCP("stateless_shopping_cart_server") def get_session_id(ctx: Context) -> str: # The MCP session ID arrives as a standard HTTP header tracked by the transport. return ctx.request_context.request.headers.get("mcp-session-id", "unknown") def get_cart(session_id: str) -> list: cart_file = os.path.join(STATE_STORAGE_PATH, f"{session_id}.json") if os.path.exists(cart_file): with open(cart_file, "r") as f: return json.load(f) return [] def save_cart(session_id: str, cart: list) -> None: cart_file = os.path.join(STATE_STORAGE_PATH, f"{session_id}.json") with open(cart_file, "w") as f: json.dump(cart, f) @mcp.tool() def add_item_to_cart(item: str, ctx: Context) -> dict: """Adds an item to the session cart.""" session_id = get_session_id(ctx) print(f"[Server]: Handling add_item_to_cart for session '{session_id}'") cart = get_cart(session_id) cart.append(item) save_cart(session_id, cart) return {"status": "success", "message": f"Added '{item}'."} @mcp.tool() def view_cart(ctx: Context) -> dict: """Views all items currently in the session cart.""" session_id = get_session_id(ctx) print(f"[Server]: Handling view_cart for session '{session_id}'") cart = get_cart(session_id) return {"status": "success", "cart": cart} # --- ASGI app for HTTP, suitable for Cloud Run --- # FastMCP mounts the Streamable HTTP MCP endpoint at /mcp by default. app = mcp.streamable_http_app() 2. Standalone ADK Client (cloud_mcp_server/agent.py)​ # Filename: cloud_mcp_server/agent.py import os from google.adk.agents import Agent from google.adk.tools.mcp_tool import McpToolset, StreamableHTTPConnectionParams # Base URL of your deployed Cloud Run MCP service (FastMCP mounts Streamable HTTP at /mcp) MCP_SERVER_URL = os.environ.get( "MCP_SERVER_URL", "https://YOUR_CLOUD_RUN_SERVICE_URL", ).rstrip("/") root_agent = Agent( model="gemini-3.8-flash", name="cloud_shopping_agent", instruction=( "You are a helpful shopping assistant. Add requested items to the user's cart " "and display current cart contents accurately using your remote MCP tools." ), tools=[ McpToolset( connection_params=StreamableHTTPConnectionParams( url=f"{MCP_SERVER_URL}/mcp", ), ) ], ) 3. agents-cli Enterprise Project (support-ops-agent/app/agent.py)​ """ Enterprise Support Operations Agent equipped with Remote Cloud Run MCP Toolset (`agents-cli`). Built with Google ADK 2.0 (`gemini-3.8-flash`), stateful tools, MCP Streamable HTTP, and A2A serving. """ import os from typing import Any, Dict from google.adk.agents import Agent from google.adk.agents.callback_context import CallbackContext from google.adk.apps import App from google.adk.models import Gemini from google.adk.tools.mcp_tool import McpToolset, StreamableHTTPConnectionParams from google.adk.tools.tool_context import ToolContext from google.genai import types MODEL = "gemini-3.8-flash" MCP_SERVER_URL = os.environ.get( "MCP_SERVER_URL", "https://YOUR_CLOUD_RUN_SERVICE_URL", ).rstrip("/") MCP_AUTH_TOKEN = os.environ.get("MCP_AUTH_TOKEN", "") mcp_headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {MCP_AUTH_TOKEN}"} if MCP_AUTH_TOKEN else None TICKET_DB: Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]] = { "TCK-1042": { "customer": "Acme Cloud Robotics", "tier": "enterprise", "severity": "P1", "status": "open", "summary": "Production payment webhook returning HTTP 503 timeouts in eu-west1.", }, "TCK-2088": { "customer": "Northwind Retail", "tier": "standard", "severity": "P3", "status": "investigating", "summary": "CSV invoice export omits localized tax column.", }, } SLA_POLICIES: Dict[str, Dict[str, str]] = { "enterprise": { "P1_response": "15 minutes", "P2_response": "1 hour", "P3_response": "4 hours", "dedicated_oncall": "Yes (24/7 SRE pager)", }, "standard": { "P1_response": "2 hours", "P2_response": "8 hours", "P3_response": "24 business hours", "dedicated_oncall": "No (business-hours queue)", }, } def initialize_support_state(callback_context: CallbackContext) -> None: """Initializes default session and user state keys before the first turn.""" if "user:customer_tier" not in callback_context.state: callback_context.state["user:customer_tier"] = "standard" if "escalated_tickets" not in callback_context.state: callback_context.state["escalated_tickets"] = [] def lookup_ticket(ticket_id: str, tool_context: ToolContext) -> Dict[str, Any]: """Looks up an enterprise support ticket by ID and syncs customer tier into state. Args: ticket_id: Ticket identifier such as 'TCK-1042' or 'TCK-2088'. """ norm_id = ticket_id.strip().upper() record = TICKET_DB.get(norm_id) if not record: return { "status": "not_found", "ticket_id": norm_id, "available_sample_tickets": sorted(TICKET_DB.keys()), "message": f"Ticket '{norm_id}' was not found.", } tool_context.state["user:customer_tier"] = record["tier"] tool_context.state["active_ticket_id"] = norm_id return {"status": "found", "ticket_id": norm_id, **record} def check_sla_policy(tier: str) -> Dict[str, Any]: """Returns response-time SLA targets for a customer tier ('enterprise' or 'standard'). Args: tier: Customer support tier ('enterprise' or 'standard'). """ norm_tier = tier.strip().lower() policy = SLA_POLICIES.get(norm_tier) if not policy: return { "status": "error", "message": f"Unknown tier '{tier}'. Valid tiers: enterprise, standard.", } return {"status": "success", "tier": norm_tier, "sla_targets": policy} def escalate_ticket( ticket_id: str, reason: str, tool_context: ToolContext, ) -> Dict[str, Any]: """Escalates a high-severity support ticket to the incident engineering queue. Args: ticket_id: Ticket identifier to escalate (e.g., 'TCK-1042'). reason: Concise technical justification for the escalation. """ norm_id = ticket_id.strip().upper() if norm_id not in TICKET_DB: return {"status": "error", "message": f"Cannot escalate unknown ticket '{norm_id}'."} escalated = list(tool_context.state.get("escalated_tickets", [])) if norm_id not in escalated: escalated.append(norm_id) tool_context.state["escalated_tickets"] = escalated tier = tool_context.state.get("user:customer_tier", TICKET_DB[norm_id]["tier"]) queue = "24/7 P1 SRE Oncall" if tier == "enterprise" else "Tier-2 Engineering Queue" return { "status": "escalated", "ticket_id": norm_id, "assigned_queue": queue, "reason": reason.strip(), "session_escalated_tickets": escalated, } remote_cart_toolset = McpToolset( connection_params=StreamableHTTPConnectionParams( url=f"{MCP_SERVER_URL}/mcp", headers=mcp_headers, ), ) # Keep name="support_ops_agent" in sync with root_agent_name in agents-cli-manifest.yaml root_agent = Agent( name="support_ops_agent", model=Gemini( model=MODEL, retry_options=types.HttpRetryOptions(attempts=3), ), before_agent_callback=initialize_support_state, instruction=( "You are the Support Operations Agent (active customer tier: {user:customer_tier?}).
" "Follow this exact operational workflow:
" "1. When given a ticket ID, ALWAYS call `lookup_ticket` first.
" "2. Call `check_sla_policy` for the ticket's customer tier so your answer cites exact SLA response times.
" "3. If a ticket has P1 severity OR the user requests escalation, call `escalate_ticket` with a concise technical reason.
" "4. Use `add_item_to_cart` and `view_cart` from your remote Cloud Run MCP toolset whenever the user asks to stage or inspect items in their cart.
" "5. Summarize ticket status, SLA targets, escalations, and cart contents clearly." ), tools=[lookup_ticket, check_sla_policy, escalate_ticket, remote_cart_toolset], ) # CRITICAL for agents-cli: App `name` MUST match `agent_directory: "app"` in agents-cli-manifest.yaml app = App( root_agent=root_agent, name="app", ) Self-Reflection Answers​ Our demo MCP server writes session files under /tmp/carts. Why is /tmp volatile on Cloud Run, and what happens to a user's cart when Cloud Run scales down to zero? Answer: On Cloud Run, /tmp is an in-memory filesystem local to each individual container instance. If consecutive requests hit different horizontally scaled instances — or if Cloud Run scales the service down to zero during idle periods — the container's /tmp directory is destroyed and the user's cart disappears. What advantages does Google Cloud Memorystore (Redis) provide over /tmp files for storing MCP session state? Answer: Memorystore (Redis) provides true out-of-process persistence across container restarts and scale-to-zero events, sub-millisecond read/write latency for fast tool execution, and strong consistency across every Cloud Run container replica reading the same Mcp-Session-Id. How does StreamableHTTPConnectionParams(url=f"{MCP_SERVER_URL}/mcp", headers=...) decouple support-ops-agent from the MCP server's internal storage implementation and authentication topology? Answer: McpToolset communicates strictly over the standardized MCP /mcp HTTP protocol and JSON-RPC tool schemas while injecting authentication headers transparently at the transport layer. Platform teams can migrate the Cloud Run MCP backend from /tmp to Memorystore or enforce IAM/Bearer authentication without altering support_ops_agent's reasoning or tool-calling logic.

In Modules 32 and 33, you deployed our stateful Python support-ops-agent (gemini-3.8-flash) to serverless containers on Google Cloud Run and orchestrated pods on GKE Autopilot. Google Cloud's Agent Runtime (formerly Vertex AI Agent Engine) completes the Part 6 compute triad as a purpose-built, fully managed runtime in the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform.

documents.t: Accelerated Container Deployment with agents-cli (Recommended Best Practice): Method: Use google-agents-cli (agents-cli scaffold enhance + agents-cli deploy). Unlike legacy pickle-based packaging, agents-cli uses container-based deployment: it packages your project and Agent Runtime builds the container image directly from your project's Dockerfile—running the exact same unified uvicorn app.fast_api_app:app entrypoint that powers Cloud Run and GKE. Key Features: Automatic managed session wiring (VertexAiSessionService), built-in A2A + native :streamQuery serving, Terraform Infrastructure-as-Code (google_vertex_ai_reasoning_engine with lifecycle.ignore_changes), CI/CD pipelines (GitHub Actions or Cloud Build), and enterprise security controls (Agent Identity, Agent Gateway, CMEK). Best For: All production ADK agents, multi-environment GitOps workflows, and agents destined for Gemini Enterprise registration in Module 36. Programmatic Python SDK Deployment (vertexai.agent_engines): Method: Wrap a Python Agent in agent_engines.AdkApp and deploy imperatively with vertexai.agent_engines.create(...). Best For: Understanding the underlying ReasoningEngine API mechanics, notebooks, or custom programmatic lifecycle scripts (deploy.py, interact.py, cleanup.py). This module's lab walks you hands-on through both workflows.

Figure: Managed container execution, automatic session persistence, and governed networking in Agent Runtime. 1. Unified Dockerfile & Dual-Protocol Surface​ When you enhance support-ops-agent with agents-cli scaffold enhance . --deployment-target agent_runtime, app/fast_api_app.py configures a single FastAPI container (get_fast_api_app) that simultaneously serves: Native Reasoning Engine Contract (/api/reasoning_engine & /api/stream_reasoning_engine): Added via attach_reasoning_engine_routes(app), constructing an internal AdkApp adapter to handle native :query and :streamQuery invocations (used by the Cloud Console Playground, agents-cli run --mode adk, and Gemini Enterprise ADK registration). Built-in A2A & ADK HTTP Routes via /api Passthrough: Agent Runtime exposes your container's HTTP routes externally under https://{location}-aiplatform.googleapis.com/reasoningEngines/v1/{resource}/api/{container_path}—making both /run_sse and your live A2A Agent Card (/api/a2a/app/.well-known/agent-card.json) reachable with standard Google Cloud IAM credentials (agents-cli run --mode a2a). 2. Managed Sessions (VertexAiSessionService) — Do Not Override session_type!​ On Cloud Run and GKE, you choose --session-type (in_memory, cloud_sql, or agent_platform_sessions). On Agent Runtime, sessions are managed natively by the platform: At scaffold time, the project uses in-memory sessions locally (shared://session). At cloud runtime, Agent Runtime injects GOOGLE_CLOUD_AGENT_ENGINE_ID, and app_utils/services.py automatically upgrades the runner to VertexAiSessionService (and upgrades artifacts to GcsArtifactService when LOGS_BUCKET_NAME is set). Critical Rule: Never hardcode or pass a custom --session-type / session_type override when targeting agent_runtime. If migrating a project that sets session_type, clear it so Agent Runtime's managed session backend takes over cleanly. 3. Non-Blocking Rollouts (--no-wait & --status) and deployment_metadata.json​ Because Agent Runtime compiles your Dockerfile remotely and provisions managed infrastructure, deployments typically take 5–10 minutes: Pass --no-wait to start the rollout and return your terminal immediately, then poll progress with agents-cli deploy --status (and audit live instances anytime with agents-cli deploy --list). Separate infrastructure region from model endpoint: deploy the engine in a concrete region (--region us-central1) while injecting --env-vars "GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_ENTERPRISE=1,GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION=global" so gemini-3.8-flash resolves on the global endpoint. When the rollout finishes (synchronously or via --status), agents-cli writes deployment_metadata.json: { "remote_agent_runtime_id": "projects/PROJECT/locations/us-central1/reasoningEngines/ENGINE_ID", "deployment_target": "agent_runtime", "is_a2a": true, "agent_directory": "app", "deployment_timestamp": "2026-11-26T10:30:00.000+00:00" } In Module 36, agents-cli publish gemini reads this file automatically for zero-flag ADK registration into Gemini Enterprise!

Agent Runtime unlocks first-class enterprise security capabilities directly from agents-cli: Capability CLI / Scaffold Flags Operational Behavior & Requirements Agent Identity agents-cli deploy --agent-identity (or --no-agent-identity) Assigns a dedicated, verifiable workload identity to the Agent Runtime resource instead of sharing a broad project default compute identity. Required before binding an Agent Gateway. Agent Gateway agents-cli scaffold enhance . --agent-gateway + deploy --agent-gateway-egress <GW> / --agent-gateway-ingress <GW> Routes inbound (CLIENT_TO_AGENT) and/or outbound (AGENT_TO_ANYWHERE) traffic through a governed Agent Gateway (projects/PROJECT/locations/REGION/agentGateways/GATEWAY). Because an egress gateway performs TLS inspection, you must scaffold/enhance with --agent-gateway so the Dockerfile trusts the platform-injected AGENT_GATEWAY_ROOT_CERTIFICATES build arg. Customer-Managed Encryption (CMEK) agents-cli deploy --key <KMS_KEY_RESOURCE> Encrypts the Agent Runtime instance at creation time using your single-region Cloud KMS key (projects/KEY_PROJECT/locations/REGION/keyRings/RING/cryptoKeys/KEY). Grant roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter to both service-PROJECT_NUMBER@gcp-sa-aiplatform.iam.gserviceaccount.com and service-PROJECT_NUMBER@gcp-sa-aiplatform-re.iam.gserviceaccount.com first. For Terraform-managed staging/prod, configure encryption_spec in service.tf (keys are immutable after creation). Private VPC (PSC-I) agents-cli deploy --network-attachment <ATTACHMENT> Enables private VPC egress via Private Service Connect interfaces (with optional --dns-peering-domain, --dns-peering-project, and --dns-peering-network). 🎯 Knowledge CheckSelect Best Answer When deploying a scaffolded Python ADK agent ('support-ops-agent') to Agent Runtime using 'agents-cli', how are durable multi-turn sessions configured, and what is required before binding an outbound '--agent-gateway-egress'? ADo not set a custom 'session_type' because Agent Runtime automatically wires managed 'VertexAiSessionService' when 'GOOGLE_CLOUD_AGENT_ENGINE_ID' is injected; for '--agent-gateway-egress', enable '--agent-identity' and run 'agents-cli scaffold enhance . --agent-gateway' so the Dockerfile trusts 'AGENT_GATEWAY_ROOT_CERTIFICATES'BPass '--session-type sqlite_local' to 'agents-cli deploy' and disable TLS verification in PythonCAgent Runtime only supports stateless single-turn prompts and cannot use DockerfilesDManually edit '/etc/hosts' inside the container and run 'gcloud compute ssh' into the reasoning engine Check Answer 💡 Need a Hint?

documents.t: Container-Based Agent Runtime: agents-cli deploy packages your repository and builds your root Dockerfile on Agent Runtime, serving uvicorn app.fast_api_app:app for both native :streamQuery (--mode adk) and /api HTTP passthrough A2A routes (--mode a2a). Automatic Managed Sessions: Agent Runtime automatically upgrades shared://session to VertexAiSessionService when GOOGLE_CLOUD_AGENT_ENGINE_ID is present—never hardcode custom session_type overrides when targeting agent_runtime. Async Rollouts & Metadata Handoff: Use agents-cli deploy --no-wait and agents-cli deploy --status to manage 5–10 minute container builds cleanly; completion writes deployment_metadata.json ("agent_directory": "app"), powering zero-flag Gemini Enterprise publishing in Module 36. Enterprise Governance Ready: First-class flags for --agent-identity, --agent-gateway-egress / --agent-gateway-ingress (paired with --agent-gateway at scaffold time), and CMEK (--key) let security teams enforce identity, governed network perimeter inspection, and customer-managed encryption without rewriting agent logic.

In this lab, you will deploy our canonical stateful Python support-ops-agent (gemini-3.8-flash) to Google Cloud's Agent Runtime using agents-cli — completing the "one production agent across Cloud Run, GKE, and Agent Runtime" deployment arc and generating deployment_metadata.json for zero-flag publishing in Module 36. In Part 2, you will also peek under the hood by deploying via the programmatic vertexai.agent_engines Python SDK.

A Google Cloud Project with billing enabled. gcloud CLI installed and authenticated (gcloud auth login and gcloud auth application-default login). Python Environment: Python 3.10+. uv & agents-cli: Install uv (guide) and install the Google Agents CLI globally so agents-cli is on your PATH: uv tool install google-agents-cli A GCS staging bucket in us-central1 for Part 2 (gcloud storage buckets create gs://YOUR_UNIQUE_BUCKET_NAME --project=YOUR_PROJECT_ID --location=us-central1). Required APIs: Enable the required Google Cloud APIs: export GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT="YOUR_PROJECT_ID" export DEPLOY_REGION="us-central1" gcloud config set project "$GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT" gcloud services enable \ aiplatform.googleapis.com \ cloudbuild.googleapis.com \ artifactregistry.googleapis.com \ secretmanager.googleapis.com \ cloudresourcemanager.googleapis.com \ --project="$GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT"

In Part 1, you will enhance our stateful support-ops-agent (featuring before_agent_callback, ToolContext state tracking across lookup_ticket, check_sla_policy, and escalate_ticket, and App(name="app")) for Agent Runtime, roll it out asynchronously, inspect deployment_metadata.json, and query the live managed endpoint over both native ADK :streamQuery and A2A!

Action: From inside support-ops-agent/, enhance the prototype to add the Agent Runtime Dockerfile, FastAPI + :streamQuery + A2A entrypoint (app/fast_api_app.py), GitHub Actions CI/CD workflow, and Terraform IaC (deployment/terraform/), then sync project dependencies: # TODO: Run `agents-cli scaffold enhance .` with: # --deployment-target agent_runtime # --cicd-runner github_actions # --region "$DEPLOY_REGION" # Then run `agents-cli install` to sync the environment. Critical Rule — Managed Sessions on Agent Runtime: Do not pass --session-type (and clear any custom session_type setting if migrating from another target). At runtime, Agent Runtime injects GOOGLE_CLOUD_AGENT_ENGINE_ID and app_utils/services.py automatically upgrades shared://session to managed VertexAiSessionService. Tip — Enhancing a Plain Legacy adk create Folder: If you ever need to enhance a plain ADK folder that was not created with agents-cli (no agents-cli-manifest.yaml) and keeps its code in a custom package such as support_agent/, pass --adk and --agent-directory: agents-cli scaffold enhance . --adk --deployment-target agent_runtime --agent-directory support_agent --region "$DEPLOY_REGION" Similarly, if your security team routes outbound agent traffic through an Agent Gateway with TLS inspection, run agents-cli scaffold enhance . --agent-gateway so the generated Dockerfile trusts AGENT_GATEWAY_ROOT_CERTIFICATES. documents.t: Agent Runtime builds your Dockerfile container remotely and provisions the managed ReasoningEngine resource, which takes 5–10 minutes. Always separate: --region "$DEPLOY_REGION" (us-central1) for the regional Agent Runtime infrastructure, and --env-vars "GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_ENTERPRISE=1,GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION=global" inside the container so gemini-3.8-flash resolves on Vertex AI's global endpoint. Option A — Synchronous Deploy: agents-cli deploy \ --project "$GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT" \ --region "$DEPLOY_REGION" \ --env-vars "GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_ENTERPRISE=1,GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION=global" \ --no-confirm-project Option B — Non-Blocking Async Rollout & Status Recovery (Recommended for 5–10 min builds): Action: Start the rollout asynchronously with --no-wait, poll progress with --status, and list active deployments in your project: # 1. Start the deployment and return immediately agents-cli deploy \ --project "$GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT" \ --region "$DEPLOY_REGION" \ --env-vars "GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_ENTERPRISE=1,GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION=global" \ --no-confirm-project \ --no-wait # 2. Poll every ~60s until completion (automatically writes deployment_metadata.json when done!) agents-cli deploy --status # 3. List existing Agent Runtime deployments in your project and region agents-cli deploy --list --project "$GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT" --region "$DEPLOY_REGION" (Optional Enterprise Flags: In hardened environments, you can pass --agent-identity, --agent-gateway-egress projects/PROJECT/locations/REGION/agentGateways/GATEWAY, --agent-gateway-ingress ..., or --key projects/KEY_PROJECT/locations/REGION/keyRings/RING/cryptoKeys/KEY for CMEK at creation time.) Inspect deployment_metadata.json: Once deployment completes, open deployment_metadata.json in your support-ops-agent/ root and verify "agent_directory": "app": { "remote_agent_runtime_id": "projects/YOUR_PROJECT/locations/us-central1/reasoningEngines/ENGINE_ID", "deployment_target": "agent_runtime", "is_a2a": true, "agent_directory": "app", "deployment_timestamp": "2026-11-26T10:30:00.000+00:00" } Keep this file intact! In Module 36, agents-cli publish gemini reads deployment_metadata.json automatically to register support-ops-agent with Gemini Enterprise without requiring manual runtime ID or registration-type flags.

Part 1: Accelerated Deployment of support-ops-agent (agents-cli)​ 1. Bootstrap (or Reuse), Enhance & Install​ # Fast-bootstrap if not reusing support-ops-agent/ from Module 31/32 agents-cli scaffold create support-ops-agent --agent adk --prototype --agent-guidance-filename GEMINI.md curl -fsSL https://mauripsale.github.io/doc-adk-training/samples/part6/agent.py -o support-ops-agent/app/agent.py cd support-ops-agent # Enhance for Agent Runtime (do NOT set --session-type; Agent Runtime wires VertexAiSessionService automatically) agents-cli scaffold enhance . \ --deployment-target agent_runtime \ --cicd-runner github_actions \ --region "$DEPLOY_REGION" agents-cli install # Quick local smoke test agents-cli run "Investigate ticket TCK-1042 and escalate if P1." 2. Deploy with Region Separation & Async --no-wait / --status​ # Start non-blocking rollout (container in us-central1, Gemini 3.8 Flash on global endpoint) agents-cli deploy \ --project "$GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT" \ --region "$DEPLOY_REGION" \ --env-vars "GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_ENTERPRISE=1,GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION=global" \ --no-confirm-project \ --no-wait # Poll rollout progress; writes deployment_metadata.json ("agent_directory": "app") when complete agents-cli deploy --status # Audit active Agent Runtime deployments agents-cli deploy --list --project "$GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT" --region "$DEPLOY_REGION" 3. Live Cloud Verification via agents-cli run --url (adk & a2a Modes)​ export AGENT_RUNTIME_ID=$(python3 -c 'import json; print(json.load(open("deployment_metadata.json"))["remote_agent_runtime_id"])') export AGENT_RUNTIME_URL="https://${DEPLOY_REGION}-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/${AGENT_RUNTIME_ID}" # Mode 1: Native ADK :streamQuery contract agents-cli run "Investigate ticket TCK-1042 and escalate if P1." \ --url "$AGENT_RUNTIME_URL" \ --mode adk # Mode 2: A2A JSON-RPC contract via Agent Runtime's /api HTTP passthrough agents-cli run "Check ticket TCK-2088 and summarize its SLA response target." \ --url "$AGENT_RUNTIME_URL" \ --mode a2a Part 2: Under the Hood — Programmatic Python SDK Solution​ support_agent/agent.py​ from google.adk.agents import Agent billing_agent = Agent( name="billing_agent", model="gemini-3.8-flash", description="Handles questions about billing, invoices, and payments.", instruction="You are a billing support agent. Politely answer questions about billing and payment issues.", ) tech_support_agent = Agent( name="tech_support_agent", model="gemini-3.8-flash", description="Handles technical support questions and troubleshooting.", instruction="You are a technical support agent. Help users troubleshoot technical issues and provide clear solutions.", ) root_agent = Agent( name="router_agent", model="gemini-3.8-flash", description="The main customer support router.", instruction=""" You are the customer support router. Your job is to understand the user's request and delegate it to the correct specialist agent. - If the user has a question about billing, delegate to the `billing_agent`. - If the user has a technical problem, delegate to the `tech_support_agent`. """, sub_agents=[billing_agent, tech_support_agent], ) deploy.py​ This script initializes Vertex AI in DEPLOY_REGION = "us-central1" for the Agent Runtime control plane while injecting GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_ENTERPRISE=1 and GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION=global into the runtime container so gemini-3.8-flash resolves on the global endpoint (Agent Runtime injects GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT automatically). import vertexai from vertexai import agent_engines from support_agent.agent import root_agent # --- CONFIGURATION --- PROJECT_ID = "your-gcp-project-id" DEPLOY_REGION = "us-central1" STAGING_BUCKET = "gs://your-unique-bucket-name" AGENT_DISPLAY_NAME = "customer-support-agent" def main(): # Initialize Vertex AI SDK in the infrastructure deployment region vertexai.init(project=PROJECT_ID, location=DEPLOY_REGION, staging_bucket=STAGING_BUCKET) # 1. Wrap your agent in an AdkApp print("Wrapping agent in AdkApp...") app = agent_engines.AdkApp(agent=root_agent) # 2. Deploy to Agent Runtime (separating DEPLOY_REGION from GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION=global) print(f"Deploying '{AGENT_DISPLAY_NAME}' to Agent Runtime in {DEPLOY_REGION}...") remote_app = agent_engines.create( agent_engine=app, display_name=AGENT_DISPLAY_NAME, requirements=["google-cloud-aiplatform[adk,agent_engines]>=1.129.0"], env_vars={ "GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_ENTERPRISE": "1", "GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION": "global", }, ) print(f"Deployment complete. Resource Name: {remote_app.resource_name}") print(f"Agent Runtime ID: {remote_app.resource_name.split('/')[-1]}") if __name__ == "__main__": main() Note: Earlier versions of AdkApp accepted enable_tracing=True. That parameter is deprecated — telemetry is controlled via the GOOGLE_CLOUD_AGENT_ENGINE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY environment variable or the Cloud Console toggle. interact.py​ import asyncio import vertexai from vertexai import agent_engines # --- CONFIGURATION --- PROJECT_ID = "your-gcp-project-id" DEPLOY_REGION = "us-central1" # Replace with the ID printed by `uv run python deploy.py` AGENT_ENGINE_ID = "YOUR_AGENT_ENGINE_ID" async def main(): vertexai.init(project=PROJECT_ID, location=DEPLOY_REGION) # Get a reference to the deployed agent remote_app = agent_engines.get(AGENT_ENGINE_ID) # Create a new session print("Creating new session...") remote_session = await remote_app.async_create_session(user_id="test-user-123") # Send a query and stream the response query = "I have a question about my invoice, it seems too high this month." print(f"
User: {query}") print("Agent: ", end="") final_response = "" async for event in remote_app.async_stream_query( user_id="test-user-123", session_id=remote_session["id"], message=query, ): # Look for the final text part in the model's response if ( event.get("content", {}).get("parts", [{}])[0].get("text") and not event.get("content", {}).get("parts", [{}])[0].get("function_call") ): final_response = event["content"]["parts"][0]["text"] print(final_response) if __name__ == "__main__": asyncio.run(main()) local_test.py (Optional)​ Note that async_create_session returns a plain dict, so access the session ID with session["id"]. import asyncio from vertexai import agent_engines from support_agent.agent import root_agent async def main(): # Wrap the agent in an AdkApp object app = agent_engines.AdkApp(agent=root_agent) # Create a local session to maintain conversation history session = await app.async_create_session(user_id="u_123") print(f"Local session created: {session['id']}") # Send a query to the agent events = [] async for event in app.async_stream_query( user_id="u_123", session_id=session["id"], message="My app keeps crashing every time I open it.", ): events.append(event) print("
--- Full Event Stream ---") for event in events: print(event) final_text_responses = [ e for e in events if e.get("content", {}).get("parts", [{}])[0].get("text") and not e.get("content", {}).get("parts", [{}])[0].get("function_call") ] if final_text_responses: print("
--- Final Response ---") print(final_text_responses[0]["content"]["parts"][0]["text"]) if __name__ == "__main__": asyncio.run(main()) cleanup.py​ Run cleanup.py to delete the manual Part 2 Agent Runtime resource (keep Part 1's support-ops-agent running until you finish Module 36!). import vertexai from vertexai import agent_engines # --- CONFIGURATION --- PROJECT_ID = "your-gcp-project-id" DEPLOY_REGION = "us-central1" AGENT_ENGINE_ID = "YOUR_AGENT_ENGINE_ID" def main(): vertexai.init(project=PROJECT_ID, location=DEPLOY_REGION) print(f"Deleting Agent Runtime resource '{AGENT_ENGINE_ID}'...") agent_engines.delete(AGENT_ENGINE_ID, force=True) print("Agent Runtime resource deleted successfully.") if __name__ == "__main__": main() # Also remove the Part 2 GCS staging bucket when finished gcloud storage rm -r gs://YOUR_UNIQUE_BUCKET_NAME Self-Reflection Answers​ Why must you omit or clear custom session_type overrides when enhancing support-ops-agent for --deployment-target agent_runtime? Answer: On Agent Runtime, the platform injects GOOGLE_CLOUD_AGENT_ENGINE_ID into the container and app_utils/services.py automatically upgrades the shared://session URI to managed VertexAiSessionService. Setting a conflicting session_type is unnecessary and overridden by Agent Runtime's native session management. How do agents-cli deploy --no-wait and agents-cli deploy --status protect developer and CI workflows against 5–10 minute container build timeouts, and what file does --status write upon completion? Answer: --no-wait starts the server-side container build and ReasoningEngine rollout asynchronously and exits immediately so shells or agentic tool runners never hang or time out. Polling agents-cli deploy --status checks the operation server-side and, upon completion, writes deployment_metadata.json (remote_agent_runtime_id, deployment_target, is_a2a, agent_directory: "app"), ready for Module 36's agents-cli publish gemini. When would an enterprise security team combine --agent-identity, scaffold enhance . --agent-gateway + --agent-gateway-egress, and --key on Agent Runtime? Answer: Regulated workloads (finance, healthcare, public sector) often require dedicated per-agent workload principals (--agent-identity), centralized outbound TLS inspection and policy enforcement via an Agent Gateway (scaffold enhance . --agent-gateway injects AGENT_GATEWAY_ROOT_CERTIFICATES trust into the Dockerfile so --agent-gateway-egress can inspect outbound traffic), and customer-controlled cryptographic lifecycle with a Cloud KMS key (--key for CMEK at creation time).

Deploy with Region Separation & Async --no-wait / --status​ # Start non-blocking rollout (container in us-central1, Gemini 3.8 Flash on global endpoint) agents-cli deploy \ --project "$GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT" \ --region "$DEPLOY_REGION" \ --env-vars "GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_ENTERPRISE=1,GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION=global" \ --no-confirm-project \ --no-wait # Poll rollout progress; writes deployment_metadata.json ("agent_directory": "app") when complete agents-cli deploy --status # Audit active Agent Runtime deployments agents-cli deploy --list --project "$GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT" --region "$DEPLOY_REGION" 3. Live Cloud Verification via agents-cli run --url (adk & a2a Modes)​ export AGENT_RUNTIME_ID=$(python3 -c 'import json; print(json.load(open("deployment_metadata.json"))["remote_agent_runtime_id"])') export AGENT_RUNTIME_URL="https://${DEPLOY_REGION}-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/${AGENT_RUNTIME_ID}" # Mode 1: Native ADK :streamQuery contract agents-cli run "Investigate ticket TCK-1042 and escalate if P1." \ --url "$AGENT_RUNTIME_URL" \ --mode adk # Mode 2: A2A JSON-RPC contract via Agent Runtime's /api HTTP passthrough agents-cli run "Check ticket TCK-2088 and summarize its SLA response target." \ --url "$AGENT_RUNTIME_URL" \ --mode a2a

support_agent/agent.py​ from google.adk.agents import Agent billing_agent = Agent( name="billing_agent", model="gemini-3.8-flash", description="Handles questions about billing, invoices, and payments.", instruction="You are a billing support agent. Politely answer questions about billing and payment issues.", ) tech_support_agent = Agent( name="tech_support_agent", model="gemini-3.8-flash", description="Handles technical support questions and troubleshooting.", instruction="You are a technical support agent. Help users troubleshoot technical issues and provide clear solutions.", ) root_agent = Agent( name="router_agent", model="gemini-3.8-flash", description="The main customer support router.", instruction=""" You are the customer support router. Your job is to understand the user's request and delegate it to the correct specialist agent. - If the user has a question about billing, delegate to the `billing_agent`. - If the user has a technical problem, delegate to the `tech_support_agent`. """, sub_agents=[billing_agent, tech_support_agent], ) deploy.py​ This script initializes Vertex AI in DEPLOY_REGION = "us-central1" for the Agent Runtime control plane while injecting GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_ENTERPRISE=1 and GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION=global into the runtime container so gemini-3.8-flash resolves on the global endpoint (Agent Runtime injects GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT automatically). import vertexai from vertexai import agent_engines from support_agent.agent import root_agent # --- CONFIGURATION --- PROJECT_ID = "your-gcp-project-id" DEPLOY_REGION = "us-central1" STAGING_BUCKET = "gs://your-unique-bucket-name" AGENT_DISPLAY_NAME = "customer-support-agent" def main(): # Initialize Vertex AI SDK in the infrastructure deployment region vertexai.init(project=PROJECT_ID, location=DEPLOY_REGION, staging_bucket=STAGING_BUCKET) # 1. Wrap your agent in an AdkApp print("Wrapping agent in AdkApp...") app = agent_engines.AdkApp(agent=root_agent) # 2. Deploy to Agent Runtime (separating DEPLOY_REGION from GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION=global) print(f"Deploying '{AGENT_DISPLAY_NAME}' to Agent Runtime in {DEPLOY_REGION}...") remote_app = agent_engines.create( agent_engine=app, display_name=AGENT_DISPLAY_NAME, requirements=["google-cloud-aiplatform[adk,agent_engines]>=1.129.0"], env_vars={ "GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_ENTERPRISE": "1", "GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION": "global", }, ) print(f"Deployment complete. Resource Name: {remote_app.resource_name}") print(f"Agent Runtime ID: {remote_app.resource_name.split('/')[-1]}") if __name__ == "__main__": main() Note: Earlier versions of AdkApp accepted enable_tracing=True. That parameter is deprecated — telemetry is controlled via the GOOGLE_CLOUD_AGENT_ENGINE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY environment variable or the Cloud Console toggle. interact.py​ import asyncio import vertexai from vertexai import agent_engines # --- CONFIGURATION --- PROJECT_ID = "your-gcp-project-id" DEPLOY_REGION = "us-central1" # Replace with the ID printed by `uv run python deploy.py` AGENT_ENGINE_ID = "YOUR_AGENT_ENGINE_ID" async def main(): vertexai.init(project=PROJECT_ID, location=DEPLOY_REGION) # Get a reference to the deployed agent remote_app = agent_engines.get(AGENT_ENGINE_ID) # Create a new session print("Creating new session...") remote_session = await remote_app.async_create_session(user_id="test-user-123") # Send a query and stream the response query = "I have a question about my invoice, it seems too high this month." print(f"
User: {query}") print("Agent: ", end="") final_response = "" async for event in remote_app.async_stream_query( user_id="test-user-123", session_id=remote_session["id"], message=query, ): # Look for the final text part in the model's response if ( event.get("content", {}).get("parts", [{}])[0].get("text") and not event.get("content", {}).get("parts", [{}])[0].get("function_call") ): final_response = event["content"]["parts"][0]["text"] print(final_response) if __name__ == "__main__": asyncio.run(main()) local_test.py (Optional)​ Note that async_create_session returns a plain dict, so access the session ID with session["id"]. import asyncio from vertexai import agent_engines from support_agent.agent import root_agent async def main(): # Wrap the agent in an AdkApp object app = agent_engines.AdkApp(agent=root_agent) # Create a local session to maintain conversation history session = await app.async_create_session(user_id="u_123") print(f"Local session created: {session['id']}") # Send a query to the agent events = [] async for event in app.async_stream_query( user_id="u_123", session_id=session["id"], message="My app keeps crashing every time I open it.", ): events.append(event) print("
--- Full Event Stream ---") for event in events: print(event) final_text_responses = [ e for e in events if e.get("content", {}).get("parts", [{}])[0].get("text") and not e.get("content", {}).get("parts", [{}])[0].get("function_call") ] if final_text_responses: print("
--- Final Response ---") print(final_text_responses[0]["content"]["parts"][0]["text"]) if __name__ == "__main__": asyncio.run(main()) cleanup.py​ Run cleanup.py to delete the manual Part 2 Agent Runtime resource (keep Part 1's support-ops-agent running until you finish Module 36!). import vertexai from vertexai import agent_engines # --- CONFIGURATION --- PROJECT_ID = "your-gcp-project-id" DEPLOY_REGION = "us-central1" AGENT_ENGINE_ID = "YOUR_AGENT_ENGINE_ID" def main(): vertexai.init(project=PROJECT_ID, location=DEPLOY_REGION) print(f"Deleting Agent Runtime resource '{AGENT_ENGINE_ID}'...") agent_engines.delete(AGENT_ENGINE_ID, force=True) print("Agent Runtime resource deleted successfully.") if __name__ == "__main__": main() # Also remove the Part 2 GCS staging bucket when finished gcloud storage rm -r gs://YOUR_UNIQUE_BUCKET_NAME

documents.t: Why must you omit or clear custom session_type overrides when enhancing support-ops-agent for --deployment-target agent_runtime? Answer: On Agent Runtime, the platform injects GOOGLE_CLOUD_AGENT_ENGINE_ID into the container and app_utils/services.py automatically upgrades the shared://session URI to managed VertexAiSessionService. Setting a conflicting session_type is unnecessary and overridden by Agent Runtime's native session management. How do agents-cli deploy --no-wait and agents-cli deploy --status protect developer and CI workflows against 5–10 minute container build timeouts, and what file does --status write upon completion? Answer: --no-wait starts the server-side container build and ReasoningEngine rollout asynchronously and exits immediately so shells or agentic tool runners never hang or time out. Polling agents-cli deploy --status checks the operation server-side and, upon completion, writes deployment_metadata.json (remote_agent_runtime_id, deployment_target, is_a2a, agent_directory: "app"), ready for Module 36's agents-cli publish gemini. When would an enterprise security team combine --agent-identity, scaffold enhance . --agent-gateway + --agent-gateway-egress, and --key on Agent Runtime? Answer: Regulated workloads (finance, healthcare, public sector) often require dedicated per-agent workload principals (--agent-identity), centralized outbound TLS inspection and policy enforcement via an Agent Gateway (scaffold enhance . --agent-gateway injects AGENT_GATEWAY_ROOT_CERTIFICATES trust into the Dockerfile so --agent-gateway-egress can inspect outbound traffic), and customer-controlled cryptographic lifecycle with a Cloud KMS key (--key for CMEK at creation time).

Across Part 6, you took a single stateful Python ADK application — support-ops-agent (gemini-3.8-flash, agent_directory: "app", App(name="app")) — from prototype scaffolding and automated evaluation (Module 31) through serverless Cloud Run (Module 32), GKE Autopilot (Module 33), externalized Cloud Run MCP tooling (Module 34), and Agent Runtime (Module 35). Now comes the final operational mile: publishing support-ops-agent into Gemini Enterprise (formerly Google AgentSpace) so employees across your organization can discover and invoke it inside a governed workspace, and cataloging your entire agent and MCP fleet in Google Cloud Agent Registry. Think of the relationship like this: ADK + agents-cli = Engineering & Deployment: How you build, evaluate, containerize, and roll out agents across Agent Runtime, Cloud Run, and GKE. Gemini Enterprise + Agent Registry = Enterprise Operations & Governance: Where employees discover approved agents in the Agent Gallery, connect private enterprise data sources under strict RBAC, and audit every agent and MCP server across Google Cloud.
